Title: U-turn ends in death of undocumented foreigner in Kluang
Article:
KLUANG: An undocumented foreigner was killed when the car he was travelling in collided with another vehicle at Km73 Jalan Johor Baru-Ayer Hitam here on Tuesday night.
The victim, believed to be from India and in his 30s, had no identification or passport documents on him.
He was seated in the front seat of a Hyundai Matrix driven by a 27-year-old Pakistani man when the crash occurred at 10.11pm.
Deputy district police chief Superintendent Nik Mohd Azmi Husin said the accident was believed to have occurred when the Hyundai, travelling from Simpang Renggam, made a U-turn and entered the path of a Perodua Axia travelling from Taman Sri Bayu towards Simpang Renggam.
The Axia driver, identified as Muhammad Khairul Azwan, 28, was unable to avoid the Hyundai and crashed into its front passenger-side.
The foreigner's remains were taken to the forensic unit of Enche' Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital for post-mortem examination.
The Axia driver, his 22-year-old wife and their 2-year-old daughter Nur Arisya Sofea were injured in the crash.
The Hyundai driver, Ali Waqar, 27, also sustained injuries to his right shoulder, left leg and thigh.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Police have urged anyone with information that could help identify the victim to contact investigating officer Inspector Mohd Hanif Mohamed Salleh at 010-2317142.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit holds steady against US dollar at opening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit held steady against the US dollar at Thursday's opening as investors awaited the release of US consumer price index (CPI) data on Friday.
At 8am, the local currency was unchanged at 4.0670/0720 against the greenback from Wednesday's close.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US CPI data would influence expectations for the United States Federal Reserve's interest rate path and could weigh on market sentiment.
"There seems to be less catalyst for a stronger ringgit, especially as traders will be watching the US CPI print to be published on Friday.
"At the same time, it is a risk-off environment and traders are seeking refuge from market volatility amid higher crude oil prices. Hence, we expect the US dollar-ringgit pair to trade within a range of RM4.05 to RM4.07 today," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said Brent crude oil prices were hovering at US$101.21 a barrel as tensions between the United States and Iran were expected to escalate.
The ringgit traded lower against most major currencies.
It slipped against the Japanese yen to 2.6483/6519 from 2.6474/6509 at Wednesday's close, fell against the euro to 4.7311/7370 from 4.7275/7333, and eased against the British pound to 5.5100/5167 from 5.5043/5110.
Against regional currencies, the ringgit traded mixed.
It edged up against the Thai baht to 12.3459/3675 from 12.3579/3788 at the previous close, while it was unchanged against the Philippine peso and Indonesian rupiah at 6.50/6.52 and 232.2/232.6, respectively.
However, the local note softened against the Singapore dollar to 3.2165/2210 from 3.2150/2192 previously.

Title: Handyman charged with threatening to kill mum, burn house over RM2,500
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A handyman was charged in the magistrate's court here today with threatening to kill his mother and burn down her house after she allegedly refused to give him RM2,500.
Muhammad Ashraf Sahridon, 26, pleaded not guilty to both charges before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
The unmarried accused allegedly threatened to cause the death of his 50-year-old mother and destroy her house in Jalan Parit Kemang, Senggarang, at 8.40am on Sept 6.
The charge was framed under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation, which carries a jail term of up to seven years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Based on the police report, the accused went to his mother's house in an angry state and hurled abusive words at her before allegedly threatening: "Aku sembelih kau, kalau tak keluar, aku bakar rumah (I'll slash your throat, and if you don't come out, I'll burn the house)."
He allegedly made the threats after his mother refused his request for RM2,500.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer Kamarulariffin Nordin from the National Legal Aid Foundation.
The court granted a RM3,000 bail and fixed Sept 23 for mention for document submission and appointment of counsel.

Title: Malayan Cement stocked up against coal supply disruptions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Cement Bhd is well-positioned to weather potential coal supply disruptions from Indonesia, having secured sufficient stocks until November, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
The YTL Group-controlled cement producer's share price has come under selling pressure since mid-August amid investor concerns over disruptions to coal supply and renewed tensions in the Middle East.
"Relative to the second half of August, the latest Indonesian benchmark prices for low- and medium-grade coal released for the first half of September actually softened by 1.1 per cent and 1.9 per cent, respectively.
"Furthermore, we posit that any price gains will likely be capped by softer demand from China and India — traditionally the top two buyers of Indonesian coal — as these markets are diversifying their sourcing by importing from other markets," CIMB Securities said in a note.
Malayan Cement aims to improve operating efficiency and increase its use of alternative fuels and materials to optimise production costs.
Its coal price assumption of US$90 per tonne for the financial years ending 2027 (FY27) and 2028 (FY28) remains above the spot price of US$83 per tonne for medium-grade Indonesian coal as at Sept 4.
CIMB Securities also expects domestic cement prices to remain fairly stable.
In the first seven months of 2026, domestic bag cement prices hovered within a narrow range of RM25.30 to RM25.95 per bag.
The research firm does not expect significant swings in cement prices for the rest of the year, provided there are no material changes in the trajectory of oil prices.
It maintained its "Buy" call on Malayan Cement with a target price of RM8.50.
Following the recent sharp pullback in the share price, CIMB Securities sees an increasingly attractive risk-reward profile for Malayan Cement.
The stock is trading at 12 times and 11 times its projected earnings for FY27 and FY28, respectively.

Title: Sarikei records country's highest API reading at 194
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarikei recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in the country at 194 as of 8am today, as 15 areas nationwide registered unhealthy air quality amid the ongoing transboundary haze.
Checks on the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed Sarawak dominating the unhealthy list, with 10 of the 15 locations in the state.
Serian recorded the second-highest API reading at 188, followed by Samarahan (181), Kuching (172), Samalaju (164), Sri Aman (158), Sibu (155), Mukah (153) and Bintulu (106), all of which were in the unhealthy range.
In the peninsula, Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 166, while Johor logged three unhealthy readings at Kluang (149), Larkin (146) and Batu Pahat (143), and one at Pasir Gudang (105).
Bukit Rambai in Melaka rounded out the unhealthy list at 104.
A wider band of areas was also inching close to the unhealthy threshold, with 22 locations in the Moderate category posting readings of 80 and above, just short of the 101 mark that would tip them into unhealthy territory.
Cheras in Kuala Lumpur led this group at 99, followed closely by Seremban (98), Alor Gajah (98), Tangkak (98) and Segamat (98), with Nilai (96), Pengerang (96) and Tasek Ipoh (95).
Johan Setia in Selangor (94) followed, along with Kota Tinggi (91), ILP Miri in Sarawak (90) and Putrajaya (88).
Also in the high-Moderate range were Balok Baru Kuantan (88), Jerantut (85), Tanjung Malim (84), Temerloh (84), Seri Manjung (83), Indera Mahkota Kuantan (83), Shah Alam (82), Banting (80), Bandaraya Melaka (80) and Kemaman (80).
Haze has gripped large parts of Sarawak since late August, with Serian earlier recording hazardous readings above 300 amid persistent hotspot activity in Kalimantan and Sumatra.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.
The public can obtain the latest hourly API readings via the DOE website or the MyJAS EQMS mobile application.

Title: Kluang hospital faces manpower shortage as bed capacity expands
Article:
KLUANG: A shortage of manpower is putting pressure on Enche' Besar Hajjah Kalsom Hospital here as its bed capacity and specialist services expand to meet the needs of more than 330,000 people.
Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the hospital currently has 396 beds, with another 38 expected to be added once Ward 10B upgrading works are completed by the end of September.
"However, the hospital is now facing a shortage of manpower. Specialist services and the number of beds increased, but the workforce has not been expanded in tandem," he said following a working visit to the hospital.
Ling said some wards are currently being upgraded with full air-conditioning.
"Johor will be raising the medical assistance manpower shortages with the health ministry.
The hospital plays an important role in providing healthcare services to the Kluang district's more than 330,000 residents, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman, two sons killed in Kluang house fire
Article:
KLUANG: A woman and her two sons were killed in a fire at a two-storey terrace house in Taman Titiwangsa here last night.
The victims were identified as Noraini Ibrahim, 49, Khairul Nurhaziqq Khairulnizam, 18, and Khairul Nurhadiff, 11.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department, in a statement, said it received an emergency call at 10.44pm and despatched 14 personnel from the Kluang station who arrived at the scene about five minutes later.
"The fire involved a two-storey terrace house measuring 16 feet by 70 feet, with about 50 per cent of the house's structure engulfed in flames.
"There were three victims trapped inside the house, and all of them were confirmed dead by Health Ministry personnel at the scene," it said.
The fire was brought under control at 12.32am.
The operation involved two fire engines and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services unit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian embassy receives Ethiopian delegation ahead of Enkutatash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Embassy of Malaysia in Addis Ababa received a high-level Ethiopian delegation on Tuesday for a courtesy visit, reflecting the positive bilateral engagement between the two countries ahead of Enkutatash, the Ethiopian New Year.
The embassy, in a statement to Bernama, said the delegation comprised representatives from various Ethiopian ministries, which include Foreign Affairs, Tourism and Culture and Sport, as well as the Ethiopian News Agency.
Representing the Ethiopian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Amha Hailegeorgis conveyed the Ethiopian Government's New Year greetings to the Malaysian mission.
"The visit reflects the mutual respect that continues to underpin relations between the two countries," he said.
Malaysia's Chargé d'Affaires  Mohd Afandi Abu Bakar thanked the delegation for the gesture and extended his wishes to Ethiopians at home and abroad for a peaceful and prosperous Ethiopian New Year 2019.
He described the visit as a reflection of the friendship built between the two nations over the past year.
According to the statement, the courtesy call also featured an exchange of cultural traditions. The Ethiopian delegation presented Abebayehosh singing, kebero drum performances, and the yellow Adey Abeba flower, with performers dressed in traditional Habesha kemis.
The embassy reciprocated with a traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony and freshly made anababero, alongside Malaysian dishes including kuih kasturi and pulut kuning serunding.
The yellow hue of the pulut kuning was chosen to echo the Adey Abeba flower, in keeping with the New Year's themes of renewal, the statement added.
The statement said, the visit came almost exactly a year after Malaysia's first diplomatic team arrived in Addis Ababa to reopen the embassy, marking a year of growing bilateral engagement between the two countries.
Enkutatash, the Ethiopian New Year, falls on Sept 11 under the Ethiopian calendar, which has 13 months and runs roughly seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar.
This year's celebration marks the start of the Ethiopian year 2019.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno general assembly: Strategic recalibration, reform ambitions and the test of political renewal
Article:
THE 2026 Umno general assembly, being held at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur from yesterday till Saturday, is expected to see more than 6,400 delegates across the main assembly and the Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri wings.
Pre-assembly programmes have already addressed Islamic scholarship, Malay education, women, artificial intelligence and the digital economy.
The setting combines tradition with an attempt to frame Umno's relevance around social and technological change.
The political message is one of consolidation before expansion.
Party leaders have repeatedly described the assembly as a forum for introspection, organisational unity and preparation for the 16th General Election.
Grassroots voices gathered through branch meetings and all 191 divisions are being presented as an essential input into strategy.
This emphasis reflects a lesson from Umno's experience: electoral recovery cannot be managed solely from headquarters. Candidate credibility, local organisation, constituency-specific alliances and disciplined service delivery determine whether national branding converts into votes.
Coalition strategy remains a sensitive variable. Umno's supreme council has authorised state leaders to negotiate political cooperation with parties interested in working together at the next election, provided negotiations rest on sincerity and trust rather than pressure.
Pas leaders were also invited to the general assembly.
These developments do not establish a new national pact, but they demonstrate strategic flexibility.
Umno is attempting to preserve room for state-specific arrangements while protecting its leverage inside Malaysia's coalition system, a difficult balance between ideological familiarity, electoral arithmetic and governmental stability.
The Rumah Bangsa narrative seeks to provide an organising frame for Malay political consolidation without reducing the party's future to nostalgia.
Its effectiveness will depend on whether unity is translated into governance outcomes.
Malay voters face concerns involving incomes, education, housing, employment opportunities, social mobility and the cost of living. A revival strategy built on emotional solidarity would be insufficient.
For Umno, political identity must be connected to economic competence, credible institutions and measurable improvements in everyday life.
Governance and integrity remain tests. Shortly before the assembly, the party leadership reaffirmed the rule of law, stating that wrongdoing should not be defended and that members or leaders must face due legal process.
Such language is important, but its political value depends on consistent application.
Umno's challenge is not to communicate integrity; it is to institutionalise transparent standards for candidate selection, accountability, political financing, internal discipline and performance evaluation. Public trust is rebuilt through evidence, not declarations alone.
Generational change presents strategic pressure. The pre-assembly focus on education, artificial intelligence, digital communication and technology indicates recognition that younger Malaysians inhabit a political information environment.
Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's remarks on scholars understanding algorithms, social media and artificial intelligence, alongside his support for student intellectual participation, illustrate this shift.
Yet digital modernisation cannot mean better propaganda alone. It requires faster policy feedback, credible data, professional communication and leadership capable of engaging sceptical voters who compare claims instantly across competing platforms.
Economically, Umno's opportunity is to reconnect political representation with material security. Stability, investment confidence and national development remain important, but voters experience the economy through wages, prices, jobs, household debt and access to opportunity.
The party's institutional experience gives it an advantage in discussing administration and development, but that legacy becomes useful only when converted into contemporary solutions.
Policy credibility will require clear priorities, financing discipline, implementation timelines and measurable outcomes rather than broad promises.
As the assembly takes place, the available evidence points less to a completed transformation than to incremental recalibration.
Umno is signalling openness to localised coalition strategy, stronger grassroots consultation, renewed Malay political consolidation, technological adaptation and a more explicit governance narrative.
Its strengths remain organisational reach, institutional memory and an experienced leadership network; its weaknesses include credibility deficits, internal tensions and the risk that reform language outruns implementation.
The evidence will emerge during the proceedings, the presidential policy speech, wing debates, resolutions and closing commitments.
The research gap is temporal as well as institutional: the assembly has not yet concluded, so any definitive verdict would be premature.
The test will come afterward, when resolutions can be tracked against decisions, electoral strategy and policy delivery.
On evidence, the general assembly is best understood as an exercise in strategic recalibration with renewal ambitions, whose substance must still be demonstrated through implementation in the months that follow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: When power corrupts organisations
Article:
The famous observation that "power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely" is particularly relevant in the business world.
Power is necessary for organisations to function. Directors need authority to make strategic decisions, chief executives need power to allocate resources, and managers need sufficient authority to lead their teams.
However, when power becomes concentrated, unchecked or exercised without accountability, it can gradually undermine judgement, ethics, governance and ultimately the organisation itself.
Power does not necessarily corrupt everyone who possesses it. Rather, unchecked power can create an environment in which poor behaviour becomes easier, less visible and less likely to be challenged.
The greater the authority and the weaker the controls surrounding it, the greater the risk of abuse.
The concentration of power
One of the most significant governance risks in business is excessive concentration of power in one individual or a small group. This may occur when a founder, dominant shareholder, chairman, chief executive or family owner controls most important decisions.
Initially, concentration of power may appear beneficial. Decisions can be made quickly, bureaucracy can be avoided and the organisation can pursue a clear strategic direction. However, over time, the same concentration can create serious weaknesses.
When one individual becomes too powerful, others may become reluctant to challenge that person's decisions. Directors may become dependent on the chief executive.
Senior managers may tell the leader what they want to hear rather than what they need to hear. Employees may fear retaliation if they question questionable decisions.
The result is an organisation where authority becomes stronger than accountability.
Power can change behaviour
Power can gradually change how individuals perceive themselves and others. A successful executive may begin to believe that past achievements demonstrate superior judgement in every situation.
Confidence can turn into arrogance, and strong leadership can become authoritarian leadership.
A powerful executive may begin to believe that rules are applicable to others but not to themselves. Expenses may be treated as personal privileges, conflicts of interest may be ignored, related-party transactions may receive inadequate scrutiny, and corporate resources may be used for personal benefit.
The danger is that misconduct rarely begins with a major fraud. It can begin with relatively small exceptions: approving an unusual expense, bypassing a procurement procedure, overriding a control or asking employees to conceal unfavourable information.
If these actions are tolerated, the boundaries of acceptable behaviour gradually move.
Absolute power destroys challenge
Perhaps the greatest danger of excessive power is the destruction of constructive challenge.
Good corporate governance requires directors and executives to question assumptions, examine risks and challenge decisions. A healthy board does not simply endorse management proposals. It asks difficult questions.
But when a dominant executive controls information, influences board appointments or intimidates dissenters, independent challenge can disappear. Board meetings may become formalities rather than genuine decision-making forums.
This creates the dangerous phenomenon of groupthink. Directors may convince themselves that supporting the dominant leader is safer than challenging the leader. Eventually, everyone agrees—and nobody is truly thinking independently.
Many corporate failures demonstrate that the problem is not always the absence of information. Sometimes the information exists, but nobody is willing to challenge the person who possesses the power.
Power and financial manipulation
The relationship between excessive power and financial misconduct is particularly important.
Executives under pressure to meet earnings targets, maintain share prices or demonstrate growth may manipulate accounting estimates, accelerate revenue recognition, defer expenses or conceal liabilities.
If the CEO is sufficiently powerful, finance personnel and auditors may find it difficult to resist management pressure.
A culture can therefore develop where financial reporting becomes an instrument for protecting management's reputation rather than providing objective information to shareholders.
This is why an effective audit committee, independent directors and strong internal audit function are so important. They provide additional layers of challenge and accountability.
The role of the board
The board is one of the most important safeguards against the misuse of executive power. Directors must be prepared to challenge management, particularly when decisions involve significant financial, strategic or reputational risks.
This requires genuine independence—not merely formal independence.
An independent director who is unwilling to challenge management provides little protection. Similarly, a board may appear sophisticated on paper but remain ineffective if directors are overly dependent on management information or relationships.
The board must therefore create an environment where disagreement is acceptable. A director should not be regarded as disloyal merely because he or she asks difficult questions.
Indeed, constructive disagreement is one of the board's most valuable contributions.
Controls are necessary—but culture matters too
Internal controls, segregation of duties, approval limits, whistleblowing mechanisms and audit procedures can help prevent abuse of power. However, controls alone are insufficient.
If the organisational culture rewards results regardless of how those results are achieved, employees may find ways around controls. If senior executives routinely override procedures, employees quickly learn that policies are merely suggestions.
The strongest control is therefore a combination of ethical leadership, independent oversight and effective systems of accountability.
The tone at the top matters enormously. Employees watch what leaders do, not merely what leaders say.
The danger of unchecked success
Ironically, successful organisations may be particularly vulnerable. A leader who has delivered extraordinary growth may accumulate enormous influence. The board may hesitate to challenge someone regarded as indispensable.
Past success can therefore become a source of future risk.
The question should never be, "Has this person been successful?" It should be, "What happens if this person's judgement is wrong, and who has the authority to challenge it?"
No individual, however talented, should become more important than the governance system protecting the organisation.

Title: From construction to chips, Malaysia's data centre boom spreads
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's data centre boom is spreading deeper into the economy, creating new opportunities across construction, power infrastructure and the technology supply chain, analysts said.
It is estimated that Malaysia's data centre capacity could reach eight to nine gigawatts (GW) by 2030, creating a RM128 billion to RM162 billion market for the domestic mechanical and electrical (M&E) sector.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said about 3.8GW is already under construction or backed by signed electricity supply agreements, while another 4GW to 5GW of incremental demand is expected by the end of the decade.
The ripple effect is also being felt elsewhere in the technology ecosystem, with company earnings tracked by RHB Research more than tripling in the second quarter on stronger factory loadings.
At the same time, contractors involved in the power infrastructure needed for data centres are seeing their project pipelines grow.
THE BUILDING BLOCKS
For the construction industry, much of the opportunity lies in the M&E works needed to keep increasingly power-hungry data centres running.
CIMB Securities estimates the capital value of M&E equipment and construction at US$4 million to US$4.5 million for every megawatt (MW) of capacity, equivalent to RM16 million to RM18 million per MW.
While the cost per MW has remained broadly stable since the start of the data centre boom, rising power intensity from changing server architecture is resulting in larger job awards.
Localisation policies are also opening the door to greater domestic participation, creating opportunities for local subcontractors and equipment manufacturers.
CIMB Securities said local companies have an advantage in navigating domestic regulatory requirements.
But the growing pie is attracting more players. A shortage of large-scale infrastructure projects elsewhere has pushed more well-funded contractors into the data centre market.
Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd is among the latest entrants, having secured an RM858 million mechanical, electrical and plumbing fit-out contract for a data centre in Iskandar Puteri.
Some contractors are going a step further by developing data centre campuses together with their utility infrastructure.
CIMB Securities said this could lower execution risks for clients and improve the chances of contractors securing repeat work.
The research house maintained its "Neutral" call on the construction sector, but described the domestic data centre pipeline as a silver lining.
It retained "Buy" calls on Gamuda Bhd and IJM Corp Bhd for selective exposure to the sector.
Gamuda has about RM7 billion of data centre wins from its Springhill data centre campus. CIMB Securities said IJM, meanwhile, is supported by restructuring, potential dividend upside and earnings visibility from data centre progress billings.
But building and fitting out data centres is only part of the equation. They also need huge amounts of electricity, bringing Malaysia's power infrastructure into the picture.
POWERING THE BOOM
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) believes Malaysia's power infrastructure cycle is building faster than expected, driven by data centres, Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) capital expenditure and solar projects.
The growing pipeline can be seen at MN Holdings Bhd, whose tenderbook has reached a record RM5 billion. Tenders linked to TNB, data centres and solar projects are all at record highs.
Its existing order book stands at RM1.6 billion, providing visibility against HLIB's financial year 2027 (FY27) revenue forecast of RM1.2 billion.
HLIB expects about RM1 billion of data centre and solar projects to be recognised during the year.
More could be coming down the pipeline.
Separately, HLIB said the Data Centre Task Force had approved an additional 5GW of capacity on top of what it described as an existing 8.3GW.
If the projects progress to electricity supply agreement signings in 2027, the research house expects a significant increase in project awards in 2027 and 2028.
For MN Holdings alone, the data centre tender pipeline stands at RM1.6 billion, including about RM500 million linked to a major customer.
The remainder largely comprises one underground utilities engineering project and three new data centre developments.
Data centres, however, are not the only game in town. MN Holdings' solar tenderbook has reached a record RM400 million, while TNB still has a sizeable portion of its FY26 regulated capital expenditure programme to deploy.
The utility had spent RM5.6 billion of its RM13 billion target at the time of HLIB's report.
Large transmission projects are also adding to the pipeline. Two 500-kilovolt (kV) projects at Pakas and Ujong Pasir account for about RM1.5 billion of MN Holdings' TNB tenderbook.
Another RM1 billion comes from 132kV and 275kV projects.
HLIB's channel checks point to more 500kV projects coming to market, with another seven potentially being launched from 2027 onwards.
The research house maintained its "Buy" call on MN Holdings and raised its target price to RM4.65, reflecting the faster build-up in power infrastructure demand.
EARNINGS MORE THAN TRIPLE
While contractors prepare for the next wave of infrastructure spending, Malaysia's technology companies are already seeing an earnings recovery take shape.
Aggregate core earnings among the 12 companies tracked by RHB Research surged 206 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM154.5 million in the second quarter from RM50.5 million previously.
But the headline number masks an uneven recovery. Aggregate earnings were still 25.8 per cent lower than a year earlier, dragged mainly by weakness among electronic manufacturing services (EMS) players.
Strip out the EMS outliers, and sector earnings rose 21.7 per cent year-on-year, reflecting what RHB Research described as a broad-based recovery and semiconductor upcycle.
Eight of the 12 companies delivered earnings within expectations, the firm said. Inari Amertron Bhd and Cnergenz Bhd were the key outperformers on stronger revenue and margins.
On the flip side, SKP Resources Bhd and VS Industry Bhd missed forecasts due to weaker-than-expected revenue and margins, an unfavourable product mix and higher input costs.
RHB Research cut its overall FY26 technology sector earnings forecast by 2.8 per cent, mainly due to weaker projections for SKP Resources and VS Industry.
Excluding EMS players, however, it raised its aggregate FY26 and FY27 earnings forecasts by 2.5 per cent and 5.1 per cent respectively.
The research house maintained its "Overweight" call on the technology sector and expects the momentum to continue into the second half.
It pointed to improving earnings, positive management guidance, healthy order books and high factory loadings as factors supporting the outlook.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to fuel the recovery. Heavy investment is filtering through different parts of Malaysia's semiconductor supply chain, lifting demand for wafer fabrication equipment and automated test equipment (ATE).
This is benefiting ATE and engineering support companies, while outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (Osat) players are seeing stronger earnings from higher factory loadings.
Capital expenditure linked to AI and data centre buildouts, together with demand for power-management and automotive integrated circuits, is also supporting the recovery.
RHB Research said ATE and engineering support companies are sitting on record backlogs, while Osat players are seeing record revenue and loadings.
EMS remains the weak link. The research house maintained a neutral outlook on the segment as it bottoms out, although higher seasonal demand is expected to improve utilisation and margins in the second half.
New project transfers and mass production are expected to make a more meaningful contribution by FY27.
WHO COULD BE NEXT?
As the earnings tide turns, RHB Research sees greater opportunities among technology stocks that have yet to fully catch up.
It sees more upside among laggards and second-tier stocks where improving earnings and operations have yet to be fully reflected in valuations.
The sector is trading at about 25 times forward earnings, around its five-year mean, even as earnings are projected to grow by more than 30 per cent.
In simple terms, valuations remain around historical levels despite expectations of much stronger earnings.
RHB Research's five top picks are Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI), Pentamaster Corp Bhd, CTOS Digital Bhd, Coraza Integrated Technology Bhd and JHM Consolidation Bhd.
MPI is benefiting from surging AI server-related demand, particularly for power semiconductors. It is expanding its AI server-related packaging lines to 28 from 16.
Its new Suxiang facility is expected to begin operations in the second half of its current financial year, backed by an initial business pipeline of about US$30 million.
RHB Research has a target price of RM55.80 on MPI.
Pentamaster, meanwhile, is sitting on a record RM550 million order book, supported by medical and AI-driven factory automation demand.
It is also benefiting from demand for semiconductor testing solutions used in AI and high-performance computing applications. RHB Research has a target price of RM6.32 on the company.
Among domestic-focused software and digital solutions providers, RHB Research prefers CTOS, believing most of the negatives have already been priced into the stock and earnings are poised to recover.
Its RM1.11 target price implies 73.4 per cent upside from its last closing price of 64 sen, the largest potential upside among the 12 technology stocks under RHB Research's coverage.
At the smaller end of the market, RHB Research singled out Coraza and JHM as its preferred picks, expecting both to benefit from an earnings rebound, stronger revenue and operating leverage.
Coraza is expected to deliver two consecutive years of record revenue and earnings, supported by a larger addressable market, higher-value projects, vertical integration and a broader customer base.
RHB Research has a target price of RM1.45 on Coraza.
For JHM, the research house believes the worst is behind it, with stronger recoveries expected in its semiconductor-related sheet metal and automotive businesses.
Growth is supported by new orders from existing customers, contributions from Magna Autosystems Inc and a RM300 million Proton contract secured through its JHM Dekai Auto Lighting joint venture.
RHB Research has a target price of 64 sen on JHM.

Title: US blacklists Ecuador's 'Tiguerones' as terror group
Article:
QUITO: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday designated Ecuador's Los Tiguerones gang a "terrorist organisation" during a visit to Quito, escalating Washington's campaign against criminal groups it says are destabilising Latin America.
Rubio said the gang was "linked to narcotrafficking" as well as "attacks targeting civilians, law enforcement officers, and journalists."
"We are not talking about an ordinary mafia, nor are we talking about common criminals, we are talking about terrorists who, in many cases, possess weapons and equipment resembling the national armies of certain countries," he said.
The group made international headlines in early 2024 when masked gang members stormed a TV studio during a live broadcast, firing shots and forcing terrified crew to the ground.
Once-peaceful Ecuador has been grappling with a shocking rise in cartel violence that has seen more than 25,000 people murdered in the last three years, according to official figures.
Drug gangs from Albania to Mexico have descended on the Andean nation, vying for control of routes to take drugs from South American coca fields to US, European and Asian markets.
An estimated 70 per cent of the cocaine produced in neighbouring Colombia and Peru passes through Ecuador.
Los Tiguerones have been linked to cocaine trafficking, extortion, contract killings, arms trafficking and money laundering.
It is one of Ecuador's most powerful criminal organisations, competing with Los Choneros and Los Lobos for control of prisons, ports and trafficking routes.
They are blamed for waves of violence, including the killing of rivals, prison riots, as well as kidnapping police and prison guards.
The designation freezes any US assets the group might hold and bars Americans from doing business with it.
Rubio made the announcement during a three-nation Latin America tour designed to shore up conservative allies in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, and bolster US influence across the region.
Los Tiguerones is the latest Ecuadoran gang to be designated a terrorist organisation by Washington, joining Los Choneros, Los Lobos and Chone Killers.
The Trump administration has designated a number of other Latin American gangs and drug cartels as terrorist organisations, including Venezuela's Tren de Aragua and the Mexican Sinaloa cartel.

Title: 2027 Budget will have to impute higher crude oil price assumptions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian government will have to chalk in a higher crude oil price assumption of around US$90 per barrel for the 2027 Budget, given the latest development in the Middle East, with Iran and its proxy the Houthis are involved in a tit-for-tat attacks against the United States' assets and Saudi Arabia, putting the already precarious situation even dire.
Brent crude surged beyond the US$100 mark on Wednesday, marking its highest level in over six weeks and surpassing the key threshold for the first time since July 24 as escalating Middle Eastern geopolitical tension fuelled supply disruption fears.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said a prudent oil price assumption for the 2027 Budget would be around US$90 a barrel, given prevailing geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia.
He said the average Brent crude price stood at US$82.18 a barrel in 2023, US$79.85 in 2024 and US$68.19 in 2025, while the average price from early January to September 9 this year was US$87.59.
"Hence, for the 2027 Budget, an average price of US$90 per barrel would be a more prudent level in light of the geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia," he told Business Times.
Afzanizam said maintaining the existing fuel subsidy structure if oil prices remained around US$100 a barrel would involve a policy trade-off, with greater resources allocated to subsidies potentially requiring cuts in other areas.
"This is a critical decision as the government is also committed to ensure that the fiscal deficits and government debt level will remain contained," he said.
The latest rise in oil prices comes ahead of the tabling of the 2027 Budget on October 9.
In May, Khazanah Research Institute (KRI) estimated that fuel subsidies could reach about RM4 billion a month, or RM48 billion a year, if crude oil prices remained above US$100 a barrel.
This compares with the RM49 billion allocated for subsidies and social assistance under the 2026 Budget, which was based on a crude oil price assumption of US$65 a barrel.
Capital Economics has revised its forecasts in light of ongoing regional hostilities.
The consultancy projects crude prices will hover near the US$100 threshold through year-end should supply disruptions persist, with Middle East energy exports anticipated to recover to pre-conflict levels only by early next year.
Goldman Sachs has offered a starker assessment of the situation. The investment bank noted that Brent crude prices might spike to US$120 a barrel should maritime aggression in West Asia intensify further.
Its projection highlights heightened concerns that ongoing regional strife could jeopardize broader transport channels carrying regional energy supplies to global destinations, beyond targeting specific petroleum infrastructure.
Extended supply chain bottlenecks could intensify competition among importers for diminished output, driving market valuations upward.
Bank Muamalat's Afzanizam noted that the fiscal deficit stood at 4.2 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in the first half of 2026, above the full-year target of 3.5 per cent, while government debt was around 65 per cent of GDP.
He also said higher oil prices would not necessarily translate into a proportionate increase in government revenue, as Petronas would need to spend more on upstream activities to safeguard energy security.
He added that sourcing oil from outside the Gulf countries could also entail higher shipping and insurance costs.
"As such, I suppose the room for Petronas to give sizeable dividend payments has become limited as it needs to preserve its cash flows for investment activities," he said.
Universiti Teknologi Mara Business Management Faculty senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said a more prudent oil price assumption would be between US$70 and US$80 a barrel, with the government avoiding a US$100 assumption given the volatility of crude prices.
However, he said Putrajaya should stress-test the 2027 Budget against oil prices of US$90 to US$100 a barrel to ensure sufficient fiscal flexibility if high prices persist.
Idham said maintaining the existing fuel subsidy structure at US$100 oil would become increasingly challenging, as the higher subsidy bill could absorb a large portion of additional petroleum-related revenue.
"This could slow fiscal consolidation and make deficit targets more difficult to achieve," he said, adding that targeted subsidies would be more sustainable than broad-based fuel subsidies.
He said any additional petroleum revenue should ideally be used to strengthen the fiscal buffer, reduce the deficit and support productive investment, rather than create permanent spending commitments.
Williams Business Consultancy Sdn Bhd founder and director and economist Geoffrey Williams said a prudent oil price assumption would be between US$90 and US$100 a barrel.
He said the government could maintain fuel subsidies at that level, but only at a very high fiscal cost.
"The question is then political, to keep Budi95 at RM1.99 and the 300 litre quota and cut health, education and social protection or change the subsidies to release funds for a pre-election budget," he said.
Williams said higher petroleum revenue would offset some of the impact of elevated oil prices, but the additional revenue could be put to better use than subsidising petrol.
The competing fiscal effects of higher oil prices have also been highlighted by analysts.
In March, Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) estimated that every US$10 a barrel increase in crude prices would add about RM3 billion to government revenue, but increase RON95 subsidies by RM3.4 billion and diesel subsidies by RM800 million, resulting in a net fiscal cost of about RM1.3 billion.
CIMB Securities subsequently estimated that every US$10 increase would generate about RM3.5 billion in petroleum-related revenue, against RM3.8 billion in additional RON95 subsidies and RM1.3 billion in diesel subsidies, resulting in a net negative fiscal impact of RM1.6 billion.
The government has also said that every US$1 increase in crude oil prices generates about RM300 million in additional petroleum revenue.
In July, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong estimated that subsidies would amount to about RM3.5 billion a month if crude oil prices remained around US$90 a barrel.

Title: IAEA board refers Iran to UN Security Council
Article:
VIENNA: The IAEA board of governors on Wednesday voted to refer Iran to the UN Security Council over its nuclear "non-compliance" in a diplomatic move to pile pressure on the Islamic republic.
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel, joined by the United States, launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites.
Nuclear facilities have also been hit in the latest war, which erupted on Feb 28, and the IAEA has repeatedly urged to be given access.
The resolution, seen by AFP, was adopted by 23 votes in favour, three votes against and eight abstentions, two diplomats told AFP. Russia, China and Niger voted against it.
It "requests the (IAEA) director general to report" Iran to the Security Council and the General Assembly of the United Nations.
The resolution, submitted by Britain, France, Germany and the United States, marks the first time Iran has been referred to the Security Council in 20 years for failing to comply with its nuclear reporting obligations.
The move is seen as largely symbolic as Iran allies China and Russia hold power to veto any sanctions against Teheran.
'COUNTERPRODUCTIVE'
Iran condemned the resolution, saying it would "not bring any results."
"This resolution was passed under political pressure from the US and its allies and in our view has no basis," Iran's representative to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Reza Najafi, told state television.
He also told AFP that the resolution was "completely counterproductive."
The text notes "with grave concern... Iran's continued non-compliance with its obligations" and "reiterates its call upon Iran to urgently remedy its non-compliance."
It also calls on Teheran "to engage seriously and without preconditions in talks aimed at building international confidence in the exclusively peaceful nature of Iran's nuclear programme."
The IAEA has repeatedly said that its lack of information and access poses a "proliferation concern" and has called on Iran to address this with "utmost urgency."
IAEA head Rafael Grossi on Monday said giving the Vienna-based UN nuclear agency access to key nuclear facilities in Iran would have "positive repercussions" for the Islamic republic.
'EXERCISE IN FUTILITY'
Before the June 2025 strikes, the IAEA calculated that Iran possessed approximately 440 kilogrammes of uranium enriched to 60 per cent, which is close to the 90 per cent needed to make a bomb and well above the 3.67-per cent limit set by a 2015 now-defunct agreement with Iran.
Since June 2025, the fate of this stockpile has remained uncertain.
Israel and the United States have long accused Iran of wanting to build a nuclear weapon.
Teheran has repeatedly denied having any military nuclear ambitions, insisting on its right to the technology for civilian purposes.
Ali Vaez, of the International Crisis Group, told AFP that "some see it (the resolution) as an opportunity to add legal pressure to economic strangulation and naval blockade to turn the screws on Iran."
"Ultimately, though, it is an exercise in futility," he added, with Russia and China "likely to ensure that Western pressure hits a wall at the Security Council."

Title: Evacuations in Malibu after waves open sinkhole at Nicolas Cage's house
Article:
LOS ANGELES: People living in an upmarket coastal stretch of Malibu were under an evacuation order Wednesday after a giant sinkhole opened up on the driveway of a beachfront home belonging to Oscar-winning US actor Nicolas Cage.
The enormous hole appeared Tuesday as heavy surf – brought by the after-effects of a hurricane – pounded the exclusive coastline, which is home to some of California's wealthiest people and a host of celebrities.
Photographs of the crater, estimated to be as much as 60 feet (18 metres) wide in places, showed it contained concrete, tiles and a portable toilet that appeared to have been placed at the multi-million dollar home for use by workmen who were doing alterations.
By Tuesday evening,
the sinkhole
was around 25 feet deep, as waves from the churning Pacific Ocean continued to eat away at the coastline, lapping around the stanchions that support the house which the "Leaving Las Vegas" actor bought for $10.5 million.
Malibu city officials issued an evacuation order affecting dozens of homes in some of the most sought-after real estate in Southern California.
"The Director of Emergency Services of the City of Malibu has declared the existence of a local emergency following a large sinkhole forming near 31630 Sea Level Drive," an announcement said.
"An evacuation order is in effect for all affected properties. Sheriff Deputies have notified residents in person, and a digital alert has been issued by the City."
South of Los Angeles, truckloads of boulders had been placed along a stretch of beach in Dana Point in an effort to protect properties in a spot where seven homes have already been declared uninhabitable, with one partially collapsing into the sea.
Richard Thompson, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, told AFP on Tuesday that coastal waters were being roiled by the remnants of Hurricane Marie.
"There were some pretty significant surf and swells across area in the last several days," he said.
"At the height of the surf and swell, we had some very significant wave heights of 10 up to 15 feet (3.0-4.5 metres) in some spots, along with significant beach erosion."
This week Hurricane Lowell lashed Hawaii with damaging winds, heavy rainfall and powerful floods, blacking out power across most of one island.
A near-record-strength El Nino climate episode is warming the waters of the Pacific Ocean and promoting the formation of powerful storms.
While the warming phase is a natural phenomenon, scientists believe the human-caused heating of the climate could make its effects much larger.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gerakan treasurer quits after 31 years amid 'unease' over Pas ties [WATCH]
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Gerakan treasurer Hng Chee Wey's resignation after 31 years could signal growing unease over the party's ties with Pas within Perikatan Nasional (PN), sources say.
Hng, who has held several senior positions including state secretary and national treasurer, confirmed he had decided to leave the party after deliberating for nine months.
Sources familiar with the situation said Hng's departure could signal deeper concerns within Gerakan, with one suggesting that "this may be just the beginning".
The sources said there had been growing unhappiness on the ground over Gerakan's association with Pas, with some members questioning whether the party had moved away from its ideology and principles by not taking a stronger stand against what they regarded as Pas' "extreme" positions.
Gerakan's position within PN has become increasingly challenging as Pas' influence in the coalition has grown, while tensions between Pas and Bersatu have also complicated the alliance's direction.
The party, however, reaffirmed its commitment to PN in June, saying it would continue playing a role in strengthening the coalition.
Hng, when contacted, said he felt he could no longer contribute in his capacity.
"I can't do anything for the people who voted for me," he said.
Hng stressed that he had no issues with anyone in the party and planned to take a break from politics before deciding on his next step.
"I have no issues with people in the party," he said.
Gerakan deputy president and Penang Gerakan chairman Oh Tong Keong confirmed Hng's resignation, saying the party was surprised by the decision.
"Of course we are surprised and will talk it out with Hng.
"As far as I am concerned, there are no issues in the party," he said.
Hng's departure marks a significant development given his three decades in Gerakan and tenure in several key leadership positions.
The resignation also comes as Gerakan seeks to maintain its political relevance within PN while navigating concerns over its ability to appeal to non-Malay voters amid Pas' growing influence.
Hng, who served as national treasurer from 2018, has also contested state and parliamentary seats for Gerakan.
For now, Hng said he would take a break from politics, leaving his next chapter unwritten.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Proposal to shut 4 Redang coral sites for 2 years
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
THE Terengganu government has received a proposal to stop snorkelling and diving activities at four of Pulau Redang's 15 coral reef sites for two years to allow the ecosystems to recover.
The Pasir Akar, Pulau Lima, Pulau Paku Besar and Pulau Ekor Tebu sites are said to have suffered more than 80 per cent coral damage.
State Tourism, Culture, Environment and Climate Change Committee chairman Datuk Razali Idris said the proposal was submitted by resort operators and Reef Check Malaysia.
He said while natural causes and climate change had contributed to the destruction, human activities were the primary driver.
"In Pasir Akar, the damage to the corals is quite extensive. Areas once adorned with vibrant colours are now severely degraded.
"It is the same case in Pulau Paku Besar, where the destruction is immense. While some damage stems from natural causes due to climate change, the most severe destruction is caused by human carelessness.
"I observed several spots where anchors were dropped directly onto the corals, causing them to die."
He said rehabilitation efforts were underway, but the recovery process required time, with corals planted in 2023 having grown only about three to four inches.
He said the proposal would be brought to the higher levels for discussion with Marine Parks, the Marine Department and the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry.
He said the move was not intended to curb tourism activities, but to ensure Pulau Redang's natural assets could regenerate and remain sustainable.
Diver Abdul Muhaimin Hou Abdul Bari Hsiung, 26, expressed sadness over the declining health of the reefs.
"We hope that the state and federal governments can take swift action to ensure tourism in Pulau Redang is sustainable."
Diver Abdul Rahim Abdullah, 36, said he was disappointed with what he witnessed during a recent dive.
"When I was at Pulau Paku Besar about 10 years ago, the corals were thriving. But nearly 99 per cent of the corals are now dead and covered in moss.
"This is a treasure found nowhere else. The government and  agencies should do something to restore Pulau Redang's beauty," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Persevere and you'll succeed, says veteran-turned-entrepreneur
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
DECADES after fighting communist insurgents in Sarawak, army veteran Rahizad Abdullah believes that a soldier's duty does not end when he hangs up his uniform.
The 64-year-old urges fellow veterans to take up new pursuits, including entrepreneurship.
"Entrepreneurship is another 'struggle', just like serving in the army. The important thing is not to lose hope. Business has its ups and downs, but we must keep going. When we fall, we get back up."
Rahizad, who markets locally produced Cravia carrot chips together with his business partners, has set up a booth during the Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur yesterday.
After completing his training in Port Dickson in early 1982, Rahizad was posted to the 10th Battalion, Royal Ranger Regiment, in Bau, Sarawak, and took part in operations around Sibu.
He remembers the bonds forged between servicemen regardless of race or religion, a lesson he hopes Malaysians will reflect on ahead of Malaysia Day.
"We were united, regardless of race. We became like brothers. We knew the difficulties faced by our comrades and took an interest in their families back home," he said.
"In the military, we look after one another."
That determination has guided his efforts to expand the carrot chip business.
He encourages veterans interested in business to approach government agencies for training, equipment and other forms of support.
"If we make the effort, we can succeed. Do not run away from problems," he said.
The Armed Forces Veterans Affairs Department is providing on-site services during the assembly, including issuing veteran identification cards and accepting applications for living, education, medical, disaster-relief and housing assistance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's affluent investors embrace AI
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Affluent and high-net-worth investors in Malaysia are among the world's biggest adopters of artificial intelligence (AI) for financial and investment purposes, HSBC Bank Malaysia Bhd said.
More than half still prefer a combination of AI and human expertise when making financial decisions, according to the bank's latest survey.
It found that 85 per cent of Malaysian respondents use AI for financial and investment purposes, placing Malaysia among the top three markets surveyed, alongside China at 85 per cent and just behind India at 86 per cent.
The study, conducted by Ipsos Asia Ltd for HSBC, covered 9,993 affluent and high-net-worth investors across 10 markets.
Despite the high adoption of AI, financial professionals and institutions remain investors' leading source of investment ideas, cited by 65 per cent of respondents.
They were also the most influential factor in investment decisions at 39 per cent, more than twice the 16 per cent recorded for AI tools.
Among those who turn to financial professionals and institutions, 85 per cent cited reassurance as a key reason, while 76 per cent valued their strategic expertise.
Investors also valued their ability to spot mistakes in AI-generated data (31 per cent), provide personalised interpretations of complex information (31 per cent)  and apply judgment and validation (30 per cent).
HSBC Malaysia country head of international wealth and premier banking Linda Yip said technology provided speed and efficiency, while human interaction remained key to building trust.
She said the future of banking would depend on combining AI-driven insights with human expertise.
"By pairing advanced analytics with human relationships, we aim to support our clients with the confidence to navigate, invest and pursue growth in an increasingly complex financial landscape," she said.
Across the generations surveyed, Millennials were the heaviest users of AI for financial and investment decisions at 89 per cent, followed by Gen Z at 86 per cent, Generation X at 85 per cent and Baby Boomers at 78 per cent.
HSBC said 58 per cent of Malaysian respondents viewed a combination of human expertise and AI as their ideal approach to financial decision-making in the future.
"While AI use is high across generations, the data shows it does not remove the need for professional insights within any age group.
"For Gen Z, this includes analysing portfolio performance (61 per cent) and generating new investment ideas (57 per cent); for Millennials, the pattern is similar at 53 per cent for both tasks," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Netanyahu under fire over report he ignored UAE's Oct 7 warning
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
ISRAELI opposition leaders on Tuesday called Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unfit to serve after a bombshell report that the United Arab Emirates (UAE) had warned him before the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack.
'Haaretz' newspaper, in a report excerpted from a forthcoming book by its reporters, said UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan spoke to Netanyahu more than a week before the attack and told him that Hamas was planning a major operation.
Netanyahu's office denied the report by the left-leaning newspaper, saying in a statement on Tuesday: "No warning was given to the prime minister from the UAE before Oct 7."
The UAE Foreign Affairs Ministry said it did not comment on media speculation, but acknowledged "open and direct lines of communication" since Abu Dhabi established relations with Israel.
"When necessary, all relevant intelligence has been and continues to be communicated between the relevant entities," it said.
Gadi Eisenkot, a former military commander who has emerged as Netanyahu's top rival in the upcoming Oct 27 elections, accused the long-serving prime minister of evading responsibility for security lapses and resorting to "pathetic" excuses, such as saying he was not woken up soon enough on the morning of the attack.
"Netanyahu received dozens of warnings for Oct 7 and ignored them all. He is unfit," Eisenkot wrote on X.
Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister also running in the elections, said Netanyahu "bears personal and direct responsibility" for the deaths on Oct 7, the deadliest attack in Israeli history.
"Netanyahu cannot continue to serve in his position for even one more minute," said Bennett.
The leader of the centre-left Democrats Party, Yair Golan, accused Netanyahu of "endangering Israel".
"The stories about 'no one woke me up' are over. You knew, you ignored, you failed, you are to blame," he said in a video posted on social media.
Opposition parties have said they would quickly establish an independent commission of inquiry into Oct 7 security lapses if they take power.
Netanyahu has rejected the proposal, instead setting up a probe by his own government.
'Haaretz' said Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar, later killed by Israel, had warned a former Palestinian official that the militants were preparing "a terrifying operation" which he described as an "earthquake".
The former Palestinian official relayed the message to an Emirati adviser, who passed it on to the UAE leader, who then called Netanyahu, according to the newspaper.
The newspaper, quoting mostly anonymous sources, said Netanyahu replied calmly to the warning. — AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Apple unveils RM8,134 passport-shaped foldable iPhone Duo [WATCH]
Article:
CUPERTINO, California: Apple on Wednesday unveiled a US$1,999 (about RM8,134) foldable phone called Duo, introducing the biggest change in years in the company's flagship product.
The Duo is sized and shaped like a passport, with rounded edges. It opens into a horizontal, 7.6-inch-wide (19 cm) screen that also can be viewed vertically. There is a smaller single screen on the front, when the phone is folded. When open, it is Apple's thinnest phone, the company said.
The folding phone event, the first with new CEO John Ternus at the helm, is the most noticeable overhaul of Apple's flagship product since it removed the physical home button from the iPhone X in 2017. The iPhone brought in US$209.6 billion, or just over half of Apple's sales, in its most recent fiscal year.
[[nid:1529411]]
Apple positioned the iPhone Duo as a business productivity device, showing how it would manage Zoom calls with multiple participants and a broader view of the Slack messaging app. The Duo's larger screen will support multiple app windows at once, a move aimed at productivity that Apple has made with some of its iPads.
Ternus criticised existing foldables as awkward and poorly suited for common tasks such as scrolling and video viewing, saying the Duo was designed to deliver an iPad-like experience in a pocket-sized device through a custom hinge, dual displays with a consistent aspect ratio, and a new titanium body.
"It's entirely new and at the same time remarkably familiar. A similar size to your passport, it feels familiar to hold and comfortable to use with one hand," Ternus said.
Apple said the iPhone Duo will feature the A20 chip to drive its displays and also a new C2 modem chip designed by Apple, part of its move away from Qualcomm's wireless data chips.
[[nid:1529410]]
"Apple has created a new premium growth opportunity, opened up another revenue stream and injected fresh momentum into the iPhone business," PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore said. Shares were down 1.8 per cent  at the end of the presentation.
TERNUS EMPHASISES PRIVACY FOCUS
Former CEO Tim Cook handed over the leadership baton to Ternus at the start of the presentation with a video about how to start the event. The video ended with a closeup of Cook, who said, "Not me. That's your guy," pointing back toward Ternus.
Ternus touted the iPhone platform as a personal AI hub that focused on privacy, saying that others wanted to collect and store personal data. "Honestly, trust only goes so far when your data is no longer yours to control," he said. "That's why Apple Intelligence runs on device whenever it can."
Apple's Lilian Rincon, who oversees AI products for the iPhone maker and was recruited from Google earlier this year, described an updated Siri assistant that will work with 300,000 apps at release.
[[nid:1529409]]
Executives also showed off the iPhone 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max handsets that are the latest versions of Apple's well-known line, which do not fold. Pricing for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max starts at US$1,199 (about RM4,879) and US$1,299 (about RM5,286), up US$100 (RM406) from the starting prices of the 17 Pro and Pro Max.
AIRPODS AND APPLE WATCH UPDATES
Apple also unveiled a feature aimed at addressing growing concerns over AI-generated and manipulated images. It introduced a new standard it calls "Apple Reference Image" to prove the authenticity of the images taken with the new iPhone 18 Pro cameras and said it will also support the emerging SynthID standard for identifying images that have been created or edited with AI. The Apple Reference Image feature will not be available in the EU or China.
[[nid:1529408]]
The iPhone 18 Pro will also include the new A20 Pro chip, which brings improvements to help advanced AI models to run directly on iPhones.
The company also said a new version of AirPods would start at US$129 (about RM524) with noise cancellation, a first for its budget line of earbuds, and that a US$149 (about RM606) version would be available with extra features such as wireless charging, and on-stem volume control that would allow users to adjust the volume by swiping up or down on the stem.
Apple also introduced the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, positioning them as major health-focused upgrades. That includes a redesigned sensor system that collects heart rate more frequently than before and powers new features that gauge recovery and fitness. The company said the watches use new Apple silicon and improved sensors to deliver what it called the most accurate heart-rate tracking in a wearable.
PREMIUM PRICING CHALLENGE
Ternus previously served as Apple's hardware chief but has kept a low public profile aside from a handful of product introductions and sustainability initiatives. It will fall to Ternus to persuade Apple's customers that they need a foldable device costing about US$2,000 (about RM8,138), a new high for a global brand that has defined mass luxury.
While Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have sold folding phones since 2019, the devices have remained a niche among tech enthusiasts. But even with a steep price tag, analyst firms such as International Data Corporation expect Apple will sell every foldable iPhone it can produce and secure a 40 per cent share of the lucrative niche by the end of next year.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak channels RM100,000 to each family of helicopter crash victim
Article:
KUCHING: The Sarawak government will channel a contribution of RM100,000 to each family of personnel involved in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang.
In a statement on social media by the Sarawak Public Communications Unit (UKAS), the state government announced it will also fully cover the education fees of the victims' children who are still in school through the Sarawak Foundation.
"Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg agreed that the assistance be channelled as a sign of the Sarawak State Government's concern to help ease the burden of the families and the next of kin involved.
"The full payment of the education fees also reflects appreciation for the sacrifices of the personnel who have provided services to the people, especially the community in the interior," the statement said.
Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) announced that a Bo-105 helicopter carrying five individuals including the pilot
crashed near Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport)
, Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching.
According to CAAM, it received information about the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm and the helicopter was conducting FDS flight operations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cyberattack ruled out in UK air traffic glitch as more flights axed
Article:
LONDON: UK air travellers faced more misery Wednesday with 177 flights scrapped across the country, as Britain's air traffic control service scrambled to recover from a technical glitch which it ruled out as a cyberattack.
Aircraft tracking website FlightRadar24 revealed the fresh cancellations after 1,300 flights to and from UK airports were axed Tuesday, with tens of thousands of customers affected at British Airways alone.
Nearly all the latest flights were at London Heathrow, Britain's busiest airport, FlightRadar24 wrote on X.
The head of the National Air Traffic Services (NATS), Martin Rolfe, meanwhile said "we have at this point ruled out cyber" as a cause.
"We don't believe it was a cyberattack," he told BBC Radio.
Rolfe said NATS will be doing a "very, very thorough" investigation into what exactly caused the incident.
NATS warned in an X post late Tuesday that "it will take time to recover" from the outage.
UK news outlets reported that British Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander had summoned Rolfe to a meeting with her on Wednesday.
Rolfe earlier told Sky News that he accepted "full responsibility" but declined to say if he was considering quitting his job.
Alexander said on X that she was "seeking assurances that lessons will be learned and systems that support aviation are up to the job."
Neal McMahon, chief operations officer at Irish no-frills airline Ryanair, called for Rolfe to be fired, accusing him of having "failed UK travellers."
'Knock-on impact'
Heathrow said late Tuesday that departures had resumed, after the "technical issue" forced the airport to suspend arrivals.
But it warned that "disruption is expected to continue", asking passengers in an X post to check with their airline before travelling to the airport.
The air traffic chaos follow a technical glitch in July last year that saw scores of flights to and from the UK cancelled, prompting anger from airline chiefs.
Britain meanwhile suffered its worst air systems failure in years in 2023, with more than 700,000 passengers affected after hundreds of flights were delayed or cancelled.
Responding to the latest fallout, NATS said: "We know this is hugely frustrating and apologise unreservedly."
'Absolute nightmare'
Caught up by the glitch, healthcare worker Josie Donoghue said it had been "an absolute nightmare" at London's Gatwick airport, having had to disembark her flight to Ireland after three hours stuck on the runway.
"Getting through that airport was like trying to get out of Alcatraz," she told Britain's domestic Press Association news agency.
Liverpool, Birmingham and Edinburgh airports were also affected, while Dublin airport said it had cancelled dozens of flights.
Ryanair said more than 65,000 of its passengers had been disrupted and it had cancelled more than 50 flights.
English football club Arsenal, due to play Napoli in the Champions League Wednesday in the southern Italian city, was forced to cancel a news conference after the team's flight was delayed. — AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cluster bomb casualties near record, driven by war in Ukraine
Article:
GENEVA: Cluster munitions killed or wounded at least 1,063 people in 2025 — most of them in Ukraine — in the third-highest annual toll on record, according to a report released ahead of a conference reviewing a treaty banning the weapons.
The vast majority of the casualties — 87 per cent — were civilians, and around two-fifths were children, the Cluster Munition Coalition's annual report said on Tuesday.
The treaty was helping affected communities, "yet the rising human toll, continued and new use, production, and transfers by states not party are stark warnings that these gains cannot be taken for granted," coalition director Tamar Gabelnick said.
The highest annual toll, 1,172, was recorded by the coalition in 2022, the year that Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Cluster munitions, fired from the ground or by aircraft, explode midair, spraying smaller bomblets over a wide area.
Survivors often suffer major injuries from blasts and burns that can result in lifelong medical needs.
Unexploded bombs can remain on the battlefield long after a conflict ends.
Neither Russia nor Ukraine has signed up to the Convention on Cluster Munitions, under which 112 states parties have agreed to prohibit the use of the weapons.
Russia has long argued that cluster munitions are lawful weapons and says humanitarian problems arise from their improper use.
Ukraine has also used cluster munitions, the report found. Ukraine's military says it adheres to the norms of international humanitarian law in using such weaponry, the report added.
Iran, Myanmar, Russia, Thailand and Ukraine, none of them parties to the convention, used cluster munitions during the reporting period, said the report, which has been recording casualties since 2010.
It also found evidence of new production in nine countries, including China, Israel, North Korea, Russia and South Korea.
The Red Cross has called for more states to join the Convention ahead of a conference reviewing the treaty in Vientiane, Laos in mid-September.
"We need a larger group of states and most big military powers to join this convention," Fahad Ahmed, Legal Adviser at the Red Cross, said.
The Red Cross said funding cuts have forced it to reduce physical rehabilitation support for victims.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran says 'prohibited zone' extends beyond Hormuz into parts of Arabian Sea
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Wednesday said a new "prohibited zone" would cover waters many kilometres beyond the Strait of Hormuz and apply to ships as far as the Arabian Sea.
Iran had first announced the "prohibited zone" earlier this week as it continued talks with Oman over a temporary shipping route through the strait.
Iranian forces have restricted traffic through Hormuz, a vital energy conduit, since the start of the war with the United States on Feb 28. The US has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports.
In an interview with state television, Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi said the "prohibited zone" would cover "part of the Sea of Oman and another part of the Arabian Sea, along the route that can lead to the Strait of Hormuz."
He added that exact coordinates would be announced later.
"If a vessel enters that area without coordination, it will be subject to our sanctions," he said.
"It means, for example, that if it later wants to come and use the Strait of Hormuz, if it wants to receive services somewhere, such as insurance or other related services, we will refrain from providing those services," he continued.
Tehran has demanded that vessels seek permission to transit the strait, insisting there will be no return to the pre-war system of unrestricted navigation.
On Tuesday, Iranian forces said they struck 10 vessels that attempted to cross Hormuz without coordination.
US President Donald Trump said in recent days American forces have helped facilitate the passage of vessels through the strait, "averaging 30 ships a night."
Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Sunday that the US tries each night to help five or six ships through, "and usually these ships get hit."
In his remarks Wednesday, Mohebi said the war with the United States could end if Washington halts "renewed threats, withdraws the Israeli regime's army from Lebanon and ends the blockade of Yemen", in reference to the Saudi-led coalition's decade-long restrictions on ports and airports run by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.
He further urged the US to "release US$24 billion in Iran's frozen assets, and refrain from any interference in the country's nuclear and missile capabilities."
Iran has repeatedly insisted that it will not reopen Hormuz until the US meets its demands.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Spain records 61 heatwave days in 2026, highest on record
Article:
MADRID: Spain recorded 61 days under heatwave conditions across the mainland and Balearic Islands in 2026, the highest number on record and far above the previous peak of 41 days in 2022, national weather agency AEMET said on Wednesday.
Spain also experienced its hottest summer since records began in 1961, with an average temperature of 24.5 degrees Celsius, 0.3 degrees above the previous record set in 2025 and 2.4 degrees above the 1991-2020 average.
Four heatwaves affected mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands, including a six-day episode in early September, AEMET said, meaning that Spain experienced extremely high temperatures on approximately two out of every three days of the summer.
The most intense heatwave, lasting most of July, affected 37 provinces and a temperature anomaly of 3.9C was recorded.
The July and August heatwaves, lasting 23 and 24 days respectively, were among the longest on record since at least 1975.
The September episode affected 16 provinces and was the fifth heatwave recorded in that month since records began.
The Canary Islands experienced a separate five-day heatwave in August.
AEMET said the summer-like conditions extended beyond June, July and August, with July-level temperatures across large parts of Spain in late May and the heatwave during the meteorological autumn in September.
Spain's 10 hottest summers on record have all occurred in the 21st century, while seven of the eight hottest have occurred since 2015.
Data on the Health Ministry's daily mortality monitoring system MoMo showed that 5,234 people are thought to have died from heat-related causes between May 15 and Aug 31, the highest toll recorded for the summer period since the monitoring system was launched in 2015.
Scientists say extreme weather events are becoming more frequent due to human-caused climate change.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Covenant unveils low-cost cruise missile with US$150m in orders
Article:
WASHINGTON: Defence startup Covenant on Wednesday unveiled a heavy-payload, long-range cruise missile it says can be quickly mass-produced at a relatively low cost, in the latest challenge to major US weapons makers from some of Silicon Valley's biggest investors.
The announcement from Covenant after two years of development coincides with efforts by the US and its allies to restock missile inventories with less expensive and plentiful long-range precision-strike missiles after the war in Iran depleted stocks of the critical armaments.
