Its missile, called Anthem, is a ground-launched cruise missile carrying a payload of more than 200kg. In a fight, it would be used in high volumes to work alongside other long-range missiles like the 1,609km range Tomahawk cruise missile produced by RTX's Raytheon unit and the 965km Lockheed Martin Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile-Extended Range (JASSM-ER).
Comparable weapons from the biggest defence contractors are "being built in small quantities at really high prices. And so we set out to change that," Michael Kaufman, Covenant's co-founder and CEO, told Reuters in an interview.
The company, founded in 2024, has raised just over US$250 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux, 8VC, Aleph and Lightspeed, and now employs more than 200 people across the US, Germany and Israel.
Anthem is powered by a solid rocket motor for takeoff and a heavy-fuel jet engine for cruise flight. Covenant says it has flown the missile more than 200 times over the past year in tests.
Executives said the missile was built with an eye toward the Pacific. "We were designed for the China fight," said Covenant President Abby Denburg.
Military planners envision using ground-launched weapons designed to strike from allied islands near China, such as the Philippines — a stretch of roughly 3218km that would put Chinese targets within range without relying on manned aircraft or naval strike groups.
Covenant is targeting a mid-six-figure price per missile once at full-rate production. The company has already booked roughly US$150 million in orders and expects to begin generating revenue in 2027 as deliveries ramp up.
An international customer is due to begin taking delivery of German-built Anthems by the end of this year, with US Army deliveries expected in 2027, executives said.
New defence companies often struggle to gain traction as they take on vested interests with new technologies and can run into significant hurdles delivering their products, especially in big quantities.
Covenant said it deliberately avoided sole-source suppliers, lining up three solid-rocket-motor providers with a fourth in the works, and locking in long-term agreements for more than 4,000 jet engines over the next two years.
The company's Dallas plant, spanning 105,000 square feet, opens on Wednesday and is expected to reach full-rate production of 5,000 missiles a year.
Covenant operates a similar-sized facility in Saxony, Germany, which will also have a 5,000-unit-per-year capacity. A smaller site in northern Israel will make 2,000 units a year.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal turns to drones to deliver flood relief
Article:
DEVIGHAT: With roads and bridges destroyed and helicopters busy with search and rescue operations after last month's devastating floods, Nepal's army is turning to drones to deliver relief to displaced people.
At least 1,367 people are confirmed dead and more than 5,000 are missing in Nepal since a Himalayan glacier broke off near the Nepal-China border in late August and caused devastation along rivers further downstream.
"Most of our helicopters are busy with rescue operations. There is no other way to send food, essentials, medicine and fuel, except for drones, which are the best option to utilise, and we should prioritise them more," said Santosh Budhathoki, a contract drone pilot for the Nepal army.
Drones are used over distances of up to 3 to 4 kilometres and can haul up to 60 kilogrammes at a time and they are already making an impact for affected communities in dire need of aid, he said.
The army is now making around 10-16 aid deliveries a day with a fleet of four DJI FlyCart 100 drones, all donated from China as part of a recent aid package.
In addition to aid delivery, drones have also been used to move the bodies of flood victims in some affected areas, while reconnaissance drones have also been heavily used in search and rescue operations.
"We've been operating back and forth early in the morning. So yes, it is quite hectic, because we need to have this thing right now," said Milan Pandey of the drone operating company, Airlift Technology.
"Nepal has this geography, this terrain where drones would be really faster, quicker and cheaper," Pandey said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Imelda Marcos US$200m graft case dismissed by Philippine Supreme Court
Article:
MANILA: The Philippine Supreme Court tossed out a graft case against former first lady Imelda Marcos that had languished in the courts for years, documents released on Wednesday show.
Marcos, 97, fled to the United States in 1986 with husband Ferdinand Marcos, who, along with his cronies, was accused of pilfering US$10 billion from the Philippines after a people's uprising ended his 20-year rule.
The former dictator died in 1989 while still in exile, but his heirs later returned to the country, allowing Imelda to see son Ferdinand Marcos Jr. become the country's president in 2022.
The 2018 verdict from the anti-graft Sandiganbayan court had ordered her to serve a minimum of six years behind bars over charges that the Marcoses funnelled roughly US$200 million through Swiss foundations decades ago.
The former first lady, famed for her lavish lifestyle, swiftly filed an appeal.
On Wednesday, court documents revealed the Supreme Court dismissed the case more than two months ago.
"In sum, the relevant Swiss documents were not properly authenticated," the court said in its ruling dated June 10.
"The prosecution was not able to present any credible witness who could have attested to the genuineness and due execution of the documents."
The case is not the first against Imelda Marcos to be overturned by the Supreme Court.
In 1993, it overturned a 24-year jail sentence – also on graft charges. She went on to run for Congress and win while her appeal was underway.
The family's notoriety stems back to Ferdinand Marcos declaring martial law in 1972. That allowed him to shutter the legislature, muzzle the free press and jail or kill those who dared to oppose his dictatorship.
In the decades since Marcos's ouster, the effort to recover the pilfered money has been halting and uneven.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK police expand donations probe into Farage's Reform party
Article:
LONDON: British police said Wednesday they had widened a criminal investigation into allegations that Nigel Farage's hard-right Reform UK party accepted illegal donations following new claims last week.
The announcement increases pressure on Farage, who has endured months of intense scrutiny over Reform's financial arrangements which has coincided with the party losing its lead in opinion polls.
Farage and his hard-right, anti-immigration party deny any impropriety.
The move by London's Metropolitan Police follows undercover footage aired by Channel 4 News last Thursday that showed Reform figures discussing steps to secure a foreign donation, which is banned under UK electoral law.
The sting prompted two senior party officials – policy head James Orr and Farage's longtime aide Dan Jukes – to resign and overshadowed the party's annual conference in Birmingham.
The Met has previously confirmed that it launched an investigation last year into financial gifts made to Reform before the 2024 general election.
On Wednesday, it said the fresh claims in the sting – carried out by undercover reporters for investigative journalism group Verbatim – would now be probed as part of that investigation.
"Detectives have assessed the information provided and determined that there are potential offences requiring investigation," said a spokesperson said, adding that they pertain to potential violations of electoral law.
British law states that permissible donations to a UK political party must be made by UK-registered voters, or a company registered in the UK.
The spokesperson added that "no arrests have been made, and no one has been interviewed under caution, in relation to the latest allegations."
A spokesman for Reform said in a statement sent to AFP:
"Reform UK denies any wrongdoing and will fully cooperate with the investigation. We won't be commenting further while a live investigation is underway."
The Met launched its investigation in February 2025 following a referral from the Electoral Commission, which oversees elections in Britain.
Parliament's corruption watchdog is investigating a £5-million (US$6.7-million) gift from British crypto-currency billionaire Christopher Harborne to Farage, who insists the money was for his security.
Farage is also facing scrutiny over alleged financial support provided by a convicted fraudster, George Cottrell.
Reform's dip in opinion polls has coincided with a bounce for the ruling centre-left Labour party since Andy Burnham became prime minister in July.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NRD: 365 foreigners charged over fake MyKad, birth certificate offences in eight months
Article:
PORT KLANG, Sept 10 — The National Registration Department (NRD) disclosed that 365 foreigners were charged in court over MyKad and birth certificate fraud between January and August this year.
Enforcement director Mazhad Abdul Aziz said 738 joint operations were conducted with various agencies nationwide, including raids on premises and factories to detect the use of fraudulent identification documents.
“Of that number, 286 cases involved the use of fake identity cards or cards belonging to others, while another 79 were linked to forged birth certificates.
“Most of those arrested were Indonesian and Filipino nationals,” he told reporters after leading Ops Layar at a printing factory in Bandar Sultan Suleiman here last night.
Mazhad added that the prosecutions were carried out under the National Registration Regulations 1990 and the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1957 (Act 299).
“We will continue to mount integrated and targeted enforcement operations to crack down on such activities,” he emphasised.
Meanwhile, he said Ops Layar, which ran for four hours starting at 5.00 pm, involved 52 NRD personnel from Putrajaya, Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, as well as 15 officers from the Malaysian Immigration Department in Putrajaya and the Selangor Department of Labour.
“A total of 195 individuals were inspected, including 63 locals who were found to possess valid identity cards.
“Three women, aged between 21 and 37, believed to be Indonesian nationals, were detained on suspicion of using counterfeit identity cards or cards belonging to others to secure employment at the factory,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Man found dead with hands, feet tied inside sewage tank in Nibong Tebal
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL, Sept 10 — Police discovered a man’s body at a house in Lorong 7, Taman Seri Bistari here today.
Seberang Perai Selatan deputy police chief DSP Mohd Norazmi Abd Ghapar said the deceased’s identity is being verified and a post-mortem will be conducted to determine the cause of death.
“Police are conducting further investigations. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder,” he said in a statement last night.
He advised the public not to speculate or spread unverified information that could affect the investigation.
It is understood that the body, believed to be a man in his 50s, was found with hands and feet tied inside a sewage tank behind a single-storey terrace house near the kitchen.
The case is believed to be connected to a missing person’s report made on Sept 7. — Bernama

Title: Tok Mat: ‘Rumah Bangsa’ should anchor Malay unity, but Umno won’t form new political alliance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno is open to Malay unity at any time, but any such cooperation must be sincere, strategic and anchored by the concept of “Rumah Bangsa”, said party deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
Mohamad, better known as Tok Mat, said Umno remained open to working with Malay parties regardless of their political ideology, provided the cooperation was based on a clear understanding of the interests and future of the Malay community.
“Umno is open to Malay unity at any time. We are open to cooperation with all Malay parties, regardless of their ideology,” he said in his speech at the simultaneous opening of the Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri Umno general assemblies here last night.
However, Mohamad said such cooperation must not be driven by seasonal political considerations or short-term gains.
He said Umno’s approach to Malay unity must instead be guided by the concept of “Rumah Bangsa”, which he described as a platform for the broader interests of the Malay community.
He added that the party did not need to establish new political alliances and would remain with Barisan Nasional, while maintaining flexibility in its cooperation with other parties.
Mohamad said that the party’s experience showed that political cooperation could provide short-term benefits, but would not necessarily strengthen Umno’s position in the long term if the party became dependent on others.
“We must build our own strength. We must have our own solid Malay support base,” he said.
Mohamad said Umno’s recent victories in Johor and Negri Sembilan showed that Malay voters could once again place their trust in the party, but warned that the support should not be taken for granted.
He said the party’s priority now was to consolidate that support while remaining open to cooperation that could strengthen Malay unity and political stability.

Title: Remains of doctor killed in Sarawak helicopter crash to be buried in Kota Bharu after forensic procedures
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 10 — The remains of Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, one of five killed in a helicopter crash in Sarawak, are expected to be buried at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery here upon completion of forensic procedures.
Her father, Kamarudin Salleh, 69, said funeral prayers for Dr Ainul would be held at Masjid Al Karamah in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa.
“I have contacted the mosque management to make early preparations for the burial,” he told Bernama last night.
On when her remains would be flown from Miri to Kota Bharu, he said the matter had yet to be finalised.
Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) stated that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching.
According to CAAM, the helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) mission when the incident occurred.
Meanwhile, Miri Division Resident Galong Luang, who is also Miri Division Disaster Management Committee chairman, confirmed that all five aboard the helicopter died in the crash at about 3.40 pm yesterday.
The victims were pilot Capt Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — Bernama

Title: Mother and two sons found dead after being trapped in Kluang house fire
Article:
KLUANG, Sept 10 — A mother and her two sons were killed in a fire at a two-storey terrace house in Taman Titiwangsa here last night.
The victims were identified as Noraini Ibrahim, 49, Khairul Nurhaziqq Khairulnizam, 18, and Khairul Nurhadiff, 11.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), in a statement, said it received an emergency call at 10.44 pm before 14 personnel from the Kluang Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arrived at the scene about five minutes later.
“The fire involved a two-storey terrace house measuring 16 feet by 70 feet, with about 50 per cent of the house’s structure engulfed in flames.
“There were three victims trapped inside the house, and all of them were confirmed dead by Health Ministry (MOH) personnel at the scene,” it said.
The fire was brought under control at 12.32 am.
The operation also involved two SITRAK fire engines and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit. — Bernama

Title: ‘Kayfa haluka?’: Warm Umno welcome for PAS delegates at assembly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The first PAS delegates to attend an Umno general assembly received a warm welcome from party members here last night.
Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan welcomed three PAS Muslimat delegates while opening the simultaneous assemblies of the party’s Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri wings.
“
Kayfa haluka?
” Mohamad, better known as Tok Mat, briefly asked, meaning “How are you?” in Arabic.
Umno leaders attended PAS’ annual muktamar last week, and in a reciprocal gesture, Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the party had invited PAS’ top leadership to its general assembly.
The two parties also worked together in the recent Negri Sembilan state election, where Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional won a combined 25 seats.

Title: ‘Forever centrist’: Tok Mat insists Umno won’t veer left or right
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno will remain a centrist and moderate party and will not be pushed towards the political left or right, its deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today in an assurance to non-Malays and bumiputera in Sabah and Sarawak.
Mohamad, better known as Tok Mat, said Umno’s ideology was rooted in centrism and that the party would continue to take the middle ground as a national party.
“My emphasis is that Umno will forever be centrist. Our ideology is centrism.
“Once again I repeat, Umno is a group and party of the middle and will forever follow the middle path,” he said in his speech at the simultaneous opening of the Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri Umno general assemblies here last night.
He said Umno would not lean to the left or right, but would seek to balance ideas from both sides while remaining a moderate national party.
He said the party’s political position had been tested over decades through its experience in governing the country with moderate policies, positions and priorities.
“Therefore, anyone who wants to work with Umno must accept Umno’s moderation and centrist approach.
“You cannot impose your conservative or radical ideology on Umno,” he said.
Mohamad also sought to reassure non-Malays and non-Muslim bumiputera in Sabah and Sarawak that Umno’s focus on Malay politics would not come at the expense of their rights and interests.
He said the Malays would continue to serve as the “indigenous nation” providing space and opportunities for everyone.
“We will ensure this homeland is a homeland for all, prosperous and carefully managed, in line with what is enshrined in the Federal Constitution,” he said.
Mohamad said Umno’s pledge was for a fair and united Malaysia, adding that the party would manage Malay politics maturely.
“It will in no way become a burden or threat, nor deny your rights and interests,” he said, addressing non-Malay friends and non-Muslim bumiputera in Sabah and Sarawak.
He said Umno’s vision was for a peaceful Malaysia where all communities complemented one another.

Title: Tok Mat admits Umno’s DAP ties were hard to sell to Malay voters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno has struggled to convince the majority of Malay voters to accept its cooperation with DAP in the federal Government, party deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today.
Mohamad, better known as Tok Mat, said attempts to justify the partnership had failed to soften the reservations of the Malay electorate, with longstanding perceptions about DAP continuing to shape how the cooperation was viewed.
“Look at how Umno has tried to justify and explain its cooperation with DAP in the Unity Government.
“There is no argument that can convince the majority of the Malay constituency, or soften their position, to accept Umno’s cooperation with DAP in the Unity Government.
“The reason is that it has become entrenched in the minds of Malays that DAP has never agreed with affirmative action policies for bumiputera. There is also a stigma that DAP is anti-Islam,” he said in his speech at the simultaneous opening of the Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri Umno general assemblies here last night.
He said the difficulty was not necessarily linked to the performance of the Unity Government, which he acknowledged had implemented policies and programmes aimed at growing the economy despite global geopolitical challenges.
He also cited the government’s distribution of aid, efforts to combat corruption and leakages, and reforms across various sectors, saying Umno supported these as part of its collective responsibility in government.
“However, all this is not seen as being more Malay.
“As long as Umno is seen as being with DAP, all of this will make the Unity Government appear as though it does not represent the Malays and their interests,” he said.
Mohamad said issues concerning Malay interests would continue to be a dominant force in Malay politics, with leadership performance, good policies and quality public service taking secondary consideration among Malay voters.
He warned that Umno would be seen as neglecting Malay and Islamic interests if it failed to manage the issue effectively.
His remarks come as Umno seeks to rebuild its support among Malay voters, after years of political upheaval since its defeat in the 2018 general election.

Title: Malaysia’s data centre boom: How it affects jobs, electricity and water
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Streaming a video, making an online payment, shopping online or using an AI-powered service involves data being stored and processed somewhere.
Much of that happens in data centres — facilities that house computer servers and other equipment used to store, process and transmit data.
Malaysia is seeing growing investment in data centres and cloud computing as demand for digital services and artificial intelligence increases.
So, what does this boom actually mean for Malaysians?
For households, the effects are likely to be less obvious than the headline investment figures, but they can be seen in terms of jobs and business opportunities, as well as the demand data centres place on electricity, water and other infrastructure.
Here is what the boom is all about and why it matters to you.
What exactly is a data centre?
A data centre is a facility that houses computer servers and other equipment used to store, process and transmit data.
These facilities provide the physical infrastructure behind many digital services, including cloud computing and applications that rely on large amounts of computing power.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) describes modern data centres as infrastructure that supports cloud computing and artificial intelligence services and enables businesses to access digital capabilities.
What is the big deal?
Demand for cloud computing, artificial intelligence and other digital services requires more computing capacity.
Malaysia has attracted increased interest from data-centre investors, particularly in Johor and the Klang Valley.
According to Mida, Malaysia had, in the first half of 2026, approved investments in data-centre and cloud-computing projects worth RM95.8 billion.
That was close to 44 per cent of Malaysia’s total approved investments during the period.
It also said Malaysia was ranked by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) among the world’s 10 largest destinations for data-centre projects.
Between 2021 and 2023, Malaysia approved RM114.7 billion in investments in data centres and cloud services.
Through these investments, 2,325 high-value new jobs were created in specialised areas including data science, data engineering, cybersecurity and network engineering.
What does it mean for jobs and businesses?
Data centre projects require workers and companies involved in areas such as construction, engineering, electrical work, telecommunications and facilities maintenance.
For example, Amazon Web Services (AWS) has said its Malaysia region is expected to support an average of more than 3,500 full-time-equivalent jobs at external businesses annually through 2038.
These include jobs in construction, facility maintenance, engineering and telecommunications.
As for students, the industry’s expansion is also creating training opportunities, including graduate engineering programmes and specialised data-centre technician programmes.
The industry is also creating opportunities ranging from engineers and cybersecurity specialists to data-centre technicians, electricians, construction workers and facility-management staff.
Data centres can also create opportunities for Malaysian companies to become suppliers.
These projects, according to Mida, also create opportunities for local manufacturers and service providers, including architectural, construction, engineering and electrical contractors.
The government has also been matching data-centre operators with Malaysian suppliers to strengthen local participation in the supply chain.
There could also be an indirect benefit for businesses using cloud services.
At the same time, data-centre and cloud services are able to help small and medium-sized enterprises with digitalisation by giving them access to cloud computing, data analytics and other digital capabilities.
For example, for a small business, cloud computing can provide storage and computing power without requiring it to build and maintain its own servers.
An online retailer could use cloud services to run its website and process orders.
What are some impacts on Malaysians?
The impact is not necessarily something that appears directly on a household bill.
It can be felt through jobs and business opportunities, the digital infrastructure used by companies and consumers, and the electricity and water needed to operate the facilities.
Why does electricity matter?
Data centres require electricity to operate servers and cooling systems, often continuously.
As more facilities come online, their electricity demand becomes part of the country’s overall power-planning requirements.
Parliament was told that the actual peak electricity demand from all data centres in Peninsular Malaysia was 849MW as of December 2025, and this was projected to rise to 4,811MW by 2030.
To meet overall electricity demand in Peninsular Malaysia, including demand from data centres, the government has planned new generation capacity of up to 9,600MW, expected to come online between 2028 and 2031.
The additional capacity will also replace existing power plants expected to retire by 2030.
This does not mean data centres automatically cause household electricity bills to rise.
It is how additional demand is incorporated into electricity planning and how the cost of infrastructure needed to serve that demand is managed.
The government is also examining whether the electricity demand declared by proposed data centres accurately reflects their eventual usage.
As of June 2025, actual electricity consumption by data centres nationwide was 603MW, compared with declared maximum demand of 1,276MW — about 47 per cent of the declared maximum.
The government said it was reviewing these projections partly to reduce the risk of underused electricity infrastructure and costs being shifted to other consumers.
What about water?
Data centres also use water, particularly for cooling.
The latest figures — 0.47 million litres a day — given in Parliament show that data-centre water use accounted for a relatively small share of total domestic and non-domestic water consumption in the areas cited.
In Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, data centres used an average of 0.12 per cent of total domestic and non-domestic water consumption in those areas.
In Johor, data centres used 9.07 million litres a day, equivalent to 0.6 per cent of the state’s total domestic and non-domestic water consumption.
To cope, one approach is to use alternative water sources rather than relying entirely on treated potable water.
The Johor government announced in August 2025 that treated wastewater of up to 12 million litres a day would be supplied to a water-reclamation plant supporting data-centre cooling.
By June 2026, the government said the 12-million-litre-a-day reclaimed-water supply for data-centre cooling was the first such initiative implemented in Malaysia.
The Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra) has also announced an integrated reclaimed-water supply chain for data-centre operations in the Klang Valley, involving AWS, Air Selangor and Indah Water Konsortium.
What are some safeguards in place?
The rapid expansion of data centres has also prompted the government to impose conditions on new projects, particularly because of their demands for electricity and water.
As of August 2026, the Data Centre Task Force cleared projects only where power and water supplies are secured and green-compliance requirements can be demonstrated. Priority is also given to operators that support the local supply chain.
Projects must also meet Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) requirements, a measure of how efficiently a data centre uses energy.
Parliament was told that applications must meet a PUE of no more than 1.6 for colocation data centres and 1.4 for hyperscalers, while sufficient Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) infrastructure must be available in the area.
In other words, the government is not simply looking at how much investment a proposed data centre can bring, but also whether there is enough power and water, how efficiently the facility uses electricity, and how much value it can create locally.

Title: Umno president urges party to strengthen solidarity, machinery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Strengthening solidarity, streamlining party machinery and staying close to the people were among the key messages delivered by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at a briefing today, as the party gears up for the next election.
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Ahmad Zahid urged party members to be grateful for the victories in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, and not to become complacent.
“...and it is important that we continue to build and strengthen the party, and ensure that it continues to enjoy the people’s confidence,” said the defence minister when met after the briefing held in conjunction with the 2026 Umno General Assembly here.
Another vice-president, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, said Ahmad Zahid reminded party members not to become arrogant following Barisan Nasional’s (BN) victories in the two state elections.
He said the victories did not guarantee that BN would win the next election, adding that the party must continue working hard to win the people’s confidence and address its weaknesses.
“Do not become arrogant. We must continue working. We need to convince the people that Barisan Nasional has learnt a lot from its experience and that we will work to address all our weaknesses,” said the Investment, Trade and Industry Minister.
Meanwhile, Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the president’s message at the briefing focused on strengthening solidarity among party leaders in facing an increasingly dynamic political landscape.
He said the briefing was a longstanding tradition held before the Umno General Assembly and served as a platform for the president to convey his message and direction to the party leadership.
“One of the clear messages conveyed by the president was the need for all leaders to strengthen solidarity so that we can face the growing challenges of an increasingly dynamic political landscape,” he said.
Another Supreme Council member, Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, confirmed that there was no specific discussion on any formula or external political cooperation during the closed-door briefing.
He said the focus instead was entirely on ensuring the smooth conduct of the meeting, adhering to party guidelines and strengthening the party machinery in preparation for the 16th General Election (GE16).
“As usual, the president’s message before the assembly only covers party guidelines. As for cooperation, we are focusing solely on matters relating to the conduct of this meeting,” said the BN secretary-general.
Negeri Sembilan Umno Liaison Committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said the message and mandate delivered by the Umno president placed particular emphasis on internal unity as a key condition for the party’s success.
He said the directive was important in preparing the party machinery for the various upcoming elections, including state and general elections.
“There is no reason why we cannot repeat our major victories in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, provided there is solidarity and unity among Umno’s machinery and leadership at all levels,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Zahid denies N. Sembilan MB resigned amid royal dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied claims that Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has submitted his resignation amid a dispute involving the state’s royal institution.
The Star
reported that Ahmad Zahid rejected the claim when approached by reporters at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur today.
“That did not happen,” he said when asked about reports that Ismail had resigned.
Ahmad Zahid also denied being present at an alleged meeting where Ismail was purportedly made to sign a proclamation seeking the removal of Negri Sembilan Ruler Tuanku Muhriz Munawir.
“I was not there. Ismail himself has denied this,” he said.
He said lawyers who were present during the alleged signing should verify whether Ismail had signed the document under duress.
“It is better for the lawyers who were present at the signing to confirm this. We have also heard that there may be a press conference on the matter soon,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid said Umno had always upheld and respected the royal institution as well as the institution of the Undang in Negeri Sembilan.
Earlier today, Ismail said he had been made to sign the document under duress following reports alleging that several Umno leaders, including Ahmad Zahid, Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dasuki and information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, were present at the meeting.
Asyraf Wajdi and Azalina have both denied involvement, while Ismail on September 6 pledged his loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz and said he remained focused on carrying out his duties for the people of Negri Sembilan.
The controversy intensified after former Undang of Jelebu Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad on Tuesday night shared copies of a document purportedly signed by Ismail concerning Tuanku Muhriz’s removal and claimed it was signed during a meeting at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on August 3.
Maarof also claimed that the ruling chiefs had appointed Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar during a meeting on April 19, and urged the state secretary and administration to abide by the purported proclamation.
Maarof and former Undang of Rembau Abdul Rahim Yasin are challenging their removal as Undang, while Undang of Johol Datuk Mohammed Abdullah also attended Maarof’s press conference.

Title: Zara Qairina inquest: Mother’s assessment unnecessary for psychological autopsy, psychiatrist tells court
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 9 — Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist Dr Chua Sze Hung told the Coroner’s Court today that an assessment of the mother of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir was not necessary in the context and framework of a psychological autopsy.
He said the focus should be on assisting the court in determining the manner of death of the deceased, with a psychological autopsy being the way forward.
Dr Chua, who was recalled to testify, explained that an assessment of the surviving parent was not a proper clinical or methodological substitute for a retrospective assessment of the deceased adolescent’s mental state.
“In forensic psychiatry, attempting to swap the two represents a category error. A clinical mismatch that mixed up two different subjects, timelines and psychological realities. These are two distinct clinical subjects,” he said before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan when questioned by conducting officer Nahra Dollah during the proceeding.
The doctor said the mother’s assessment focuses on her current clinical condition rather than retrospectively assessing the deceased’s mental state
Dr Chua, who first testified as a witness in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina in April, said a cross-sectional psychiatric diagnosis or non-diagnosis of the mother’s current mental state was of little help in understanding the adolescent’s symptom load and final suicidal intent.
“Forensic literature warns that survivors in death inquiries can be interested parties whose recollections can be coloured by guilt, anger and shame.
“The adolescent’s own written diaries documenting her various difficulties represent the most critical uncontaminated pre-mortem data,” he added.
Meanwhile, Dr Chua said clinical psychiatric assessment is not meant to be done retrospectively or to answer the manner of death.
“I stand by my conclusion that the deceased’s manner of death is most consistent with suicide.
“I humbly submit that it is the prerogative of the court to determine the final manner of death and my opinion remains an expert opinion on the balance of probability,” he added.
Zara Qairina, 13, died on July 17, 2025 at Queen Elizabeth Hospital, where she had been admitted a day earlier after being found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel in Papar at 4 am.
The proceedings resume tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Anwar remembers Capt Zainol Afiq as kind man, pays tribute to pilot’s service (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim remembers Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, the pilot who was killed in yesterday’s helicopter crash in Sarawak, as a kind man of good character.
Anwar said he had fond memories of Zainol Afiq, who had flown him during the 15th General Election (GE15) campaign, including the pilot’s habit of shaking hands with him before boarding and after disembarking from the helicopter, as well as reciting prayers together.
He said the pilot’s service and contributions would always be remembered, and urged his family to inform his staff if they needed any assistance.
“He was a good person. He helped us a lot in our struggle. His contributions and service will always be remembered. If there is anything we can do to help, please let my staff know and, insya-Allah, I will make the necessary arrangements,” he said in a video clip of a telephone conversation with the late pilot’s father, Bee Sham Ahmad, that was shared on Facebook.
Anwar had called Bee Sham to convey his condolences, as well as those of his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail and their family, to the bereaved family.
He also prayed for Allah SWT to grant the family strength, fortitude and patience in coping with their loss, and to shower His mercy upon Zainol Afiq’s soul.
The prime minister said he would also contact the families of the other victims killed in the crash.
“Malaysia mourns their sacrifice and their selfless service to the nation,” he said.
Anwar also gave an assurance that the Madani Government would ensure that the families of the crash victims received the necessary assistance and support and that their interests were properly looked after.
Yesterday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying Zainol Afiq and four others crashed and caught fire near Long Lellang Airport in Ulu Baram.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), in a statement yesterday afternoon, confirmed the incident and said it had received notification of the crash from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.
The four other victims comprised a medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses, all from the Health Ministry. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry: Unsubsidised petrol, diesel prices rise 25 sen per litre from tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 petrol and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 25 sen per litre for the period from September 10 to 16, 2026.
The Finance Ministry (MOF), in a statement today, said RON97 would be priced at RM4.50 per litre from RM4.25 previously, while RON95 would rise to RM4.02 from RM3.77 and unsubsidised diesel to RM4.92 from RM4.67.
MOF said global crude oil prices rose significantly during the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period following renewed escalation in the conflict between the United States and Iran and increased risks of disruption to petroleum supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.
“Brent crude oil prices rose throughout the APM calculation period before reaching US$97.31 a barrel on Monday. Geopolitical risk premiums on global oil supplies also increased following continued retaliatory attacks between the United States and Iran.
“At the same time, the global market for refined petroleum products remained tight. Disruptions to refining capacity in West Asia and continued attacks on Russian refineries have reduced supplies of petrol, diesel and other petroleum products to international markets,” it said.
MOF said diesel prices in the international market also rose faster than crude oil prices due to constraints on refining capacity and declining inventories.
“After 193 days of conflict in West Asia, petroleum flows through the Strait of Hormuz and global refining capacity have yet to return to normal. If this situation persists, declining inventories and increasingly tight supplies of refined petroleum products could increase risk premiums on global petrol and diesel prices,” MOF said.
The ministry said the Madani Government would continue to protect the people and businesses from the impact of global uncertainties by maintaining targeted Budi Madani subsidies for eligible consumers.
Under Budi95, eligible recipients will continue to pay RM1.99 per litre for RON95, with the Government bearing a subsidy of RM2.03 per litre, or 50 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.02.
For Budi Diesel, recipients will pay RM2.10 per litre, with the government providing a subsidy of RM2.82 per litre, or 57 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.92.
Meanwhile, petrol prices under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and diesel prices under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) will remain at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre, respectively.
The basic monthly eligibility limit for Budi95 and Budi Diesel had been raised again to 300 litres from September 1, while eligible owners of diesel-powered pickup trucks and jeeps would receive an additional 100 litres, bringing their total monthly eligibility to 400 litres, the minitsry added. — Bernama

Title: Former Felda subsidiary CEO gets four-day remand extension in corruption probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 9 — The remand of a former chief executive officer (CEO) of a subsidiary of a federal statutory body has been extended by four days to assist investigations into alleged misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving the appointment of a developer for a project in Kuala Lumpur.
A source said the remand order, which runs from tomorrow until September 13, was issued by Magistrate Ezrene Zakaria after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made the application at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court here this morning.
“The remand application was made after the suspect’s initial remand period ended today. The suspect was previously remanded for three days from last Monday,” the source said.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, said the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009.
Last Monday, MACC obtained a five-day remand order until September 11 against two individuals, including a Datuk who is also a former director-general of the statutory body, while the former CEO, who is currently receiving treatment at Putrajaya Hospital, was remanded for three days until today.
The two individuals, in their 50s and 60s, were detained last Sunday after appearing at the MACC headquarters to have their statements recorded.
MACC has opened seven investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC). — Bernama

Title: Anwar: PM’s Cup debate nurtures confident, critical young minds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Prime Minister’s Cup Debate Competition is more than a platform for testing debating skills, serving an important role in developing young people who are confident in speaking up, think critically, and respect differing views, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
In a Facebook post, the prime minister said the competition continues the legacy of Tun Abdul Razak Hussein by providing young people with a platform to test their courage, deepen their knowledge and sharpen their debating skills.
“More than just a competition, it provides a space for young people to learn how to organise their thoughts, defend their positions and, at the same time, respect differing views,” he said.
Anwar said he had the opportunity to meet the finalists of the 51st edition of the competition after today’s Cabinet meeting, ahead of the grand final scheduled to be held at Multimedia University in Cyberjaya tomorrow.
He said he was impressed by the participants’ awareness of current developments, as well as their courage in raising questions and critically examining various issues.
Anwar said a healthy democracy was not only about having the courage to speak up, but also the willingness to listen and respect differences.
He also advised the finalists to debate firmly, confidently and respectfully, arguing without hatred and disagreeing without hostility.
The Prime Minister’s Cup Debate Competition was first held in 1974 at the Malay College Kuala Kangsar in Perak.
It was introduced as part of Malaysia’s second Prime Minister Tun Abdul Razak Hussein’s vision to nurture dynamic, intelligent, and capable future leaders among students at fully residential schools. — Bernama

Title: Azalina, Asyraf Wajdi deny attending meeting linked to alleged bid to remove Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Two Umno leaders have denied attending a meeting allegedly linked to claims that Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had signed a declaration seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz Munawir as the state’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The denials came from Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dasuki and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said,
Harian Metro
reported today.
Azalina said she was unaware of the alleged matter.
“I don’t know, I wasn’t there when he (Ismail) signed it. I really wasn’t,” she told reporters after the President’s Briefing held in conjunction with the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Asyraf Wajdi, meanwhile, stressed that he was not involved in the alleged meeting.
“I wasn’t there. I wasn’t involved, I’m not (part of the leadership) in Negri Sembilan. I’m only a national delegate,” he said.

Title: Alam Maritim Resources CEO Azmi Ahmad to be charged over Tabung Haji probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Alam Maritim Resources Bhd group managing director and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Azmi Ahmad will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow.
Based on a check of the court system, Azmi will be charged at Criminal Sessions Court 14 before Judge Suzana Hussin at 9am.
On August 17, Alam Maritim Resources Bhd, in a filing with Bursa Malaysia, said that Azmi had been remanded to assist in an investigation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
On August 15, Bernama reported that MACC had detained seven individuals comprising a CEO, a company director, a former company director and four former senior management officers of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to assist in investigations into issues raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry Report on Tabung Haji.
According to a source, a shipping company CEO in his 60s with the title Datuk was detained for allegedly submitting documents containing false material details when making payments to TH, involving the falsification of contract documents of a petroleum company for the benefit of his own company. — Bernama

Title: Hubline confirms helicopter in fatal Long Lellang crash was operated by subsidiary
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Shipping and aviation services company Hubline Bhd has confirmed that the helicopter involved in the accident at the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Sarawak on Tuesday was operated by its unit, Layang Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd (LLA).
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Hubline said the helicopter, bearing registration number 9M-LLF, was conducting a flying doctor service (FDS) flight when the accident occurred.
“The helicopter was operating a FDS flight with five persons on board, including the pilot,” it said.
The company said LLA has activated its emergency response plan following the incident and is working closely with the relevant authorities, including the Air Accident Investigation Bureau under the Ministry of Transport, while providing all possible assistance.
Hubline also said its board is currently assessing the financial and operational impact of the accident on the group.
On Tuesday, a helicopter crashed near the Long Lellang STOLport in the interior of Marudi district in northern Sarawak at about 3.40pm, killing the pilot and four Ministry of Health personnel. — Bernama

Title: Remains of five Long Lellang helicopter crash victims recovered, DNA identification to follow
Article:
MIRI, Sept 9 — The five victims in the helicopter which crashed in Long Lellang on Tuesday have been recovered, said Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah.
He said the charred remains were found in the wreckage, adding that further identification was required with DNA samples taken from family members.
He identified the victims as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
“Although we have identified all the victims, none of the remains were found intact.
“We have informed all the victims’ families and obtained DNA samples from them for identification purposes,” he told a press conference at Miri Airport here.
Mohamad Zainal said formal identification would be carried out at Miri Hospital, where the remains and tissue samples would also be sent for further examination and DNA testing.
He said police were fortunate that the helicopter crashed at the end of the STOLport runway.
“I believe the pilot may have attempted to make a safe landing as the helicopter was right at the end of the runway.
“If it had crashed further away from the runway and into the forest, it would have been more difficult for us to conduct the rescue operation and recover the victims,” he said.
Mohamad Zainal said the team departed Miri Airport at 10.21am on Tuesday for Ba Lai in Ulu Baram, with the flight taking about an hour.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said formal identification would be carried out at Miri Hospital, where the remains and tissue samples would also be sent for further examination and DNA testing. — The Borneo Post pic
From Ba Lai, the helicopter flew to Long Siut, a journey of about seven to eight minutes, before continuing to Long Lellang, where the crash occurred less than 10 minutes later.
Several witnesses reportedly saw the helicopter shortly before the crash and reported seeing smoke and flames before it went down.
Asked whether the pilot had made an emergency call before the crash, Mohamad Zainal said preliminary investigations found that the helicopter was not equipped with a voice recorder or black box.
He said the Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) would conduct further investigations to determine the cause of the crash and establish how the incident occurred.
On the helicopter’s maintenance history, he said its last maintenance was carried out on August 24.
“Following the maintenance, the helicopter could be used for up to 100 flight hours. So, the maintenance was carried out quite recently,” he said.
Mohamad Zainal said the helicopter had been used by the Health Ministry for its Flying Doctor Service (FDS) in Sarawak for about 17 years, since 2009.
During that period, he said it had conducted numerous operations supporting healthcare services in remote areas, particularly in Miri, Bintulu, Limbang, Marudi and Baram.
He described the five victims as “our heroes” who had served and provided healthcare services to people in rural areas.
A total of 67 personnel were involved in Tuesday’s recovery operation, comprising 19 police personnel, 15 Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department personnel, two Health Ministry personnel, three Malaysia Airports personnel, one representative from Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, 15 General Operations Force (GOF) personnel, four Civil Defence Force personnel and eight People’s Volunteer Corps (Rela) personnel. — The Borneo Post

Title: Umno delegates enter assembly on an election high after Johor, N. Sembilan wins, with Melaka next on the radar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno delegates arrived for the first day of the party’s annual assembly today in an upbeat mood following its back-to-back victories in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with Melaka now emerging as the next electoral target.
The mood at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur was markedly positive, with delegates turning up in large numbers for briefings ahead of the official opening of the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
BN won 48 of the 56 seats in Johor, including 36 for Umno, while in Negri Sembilan the coalition secured 18 of the 36 seats, with Umno winning all 16 seats it contested.
Umno Youth Damansara committee member Muhammad Najeeh Norazam, 33, said the two state election victories had given delegates a morale boost and changed the atmosphere within the party.
“I think the delegates’ morale is a bit more energised because of the back-to-back wins in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections.
“Personally, I think the delegates are now waiting to see what decision will be made and which direction we are going to take for the elections,” he told Malay Mail.
Najeeh said the change in mood was evident compared with earlier this year, with more delegates now turning up for the assembly following the two victories.
“So I think it is a positive mood for now. We won, and then we are hoping for Melaka,” he said.
Umno Youth Damansara committee member Muhammad Najeeh Norazam, 33, said the two state election victories had given delegates a morale boost and changed the atmosphere within the party. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Umno Ampang division information chief Mohamad Anas Mohamad Naem, 33, also said the strong turnout reflected the renewed enthusiasm among delegates.
“As we can see today, the reception has been very lively. We saw that every level of the hall during the briefing was full, with no empty seats,” he said after attending the closed-door president’s briefing.
Anas said Umno was now prepared for its next electoral challenge after overcoming what he described as considerable political pressure against the party.
“Although we know that the current political situation makes it seem as though Umno is under tremendous pressure, with various sentiments and narratives being directed at Umno, after the victories in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, and next in Melaka, God willing, Umno is now ready.
“We are on the right track and prepared, waiting for instructions from the top leadership,” he said.
The renewed confidence comes as Umno prepares to discuss its direction ahead of the next general election, with delegates expected to look beyond its recent state election victories and towards the challenges ahead.
For Najeeh, the immediate focus is clear: building on the momentum from Johor and Negeri Sembilan and carrying it into the next electoral contest.
For Junaidi Ifdam Jun, 32, from the Batu Sapi, Sabah division, he said that he can’t wait to experience the four-day assembly as it is his first time attending it.
The assembly runs from today to Saturday.

Title: RM1.25b solar hybrid project corruption case: Prosecution challenges ruling allowing Rosmah to adduce additional evidence
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 9 — The prosecution has filed an application to stay the Court of Appeal’s decision that granted Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor leave to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction in the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project corruption case.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohd Asnawi Abu Hanipah confirmed that the application was filed at the Court of Appeal yesterday.
The application for stay seeks to temporarily suspend the taking of additional evidence pending the disposal of the prosecution’s appeal before the Federal Court.
Mohd Asnawi also confirmed that the prosecution had filed its notice of appeal against the Court of Appeal’s ruling on September 4.
On August 1, a three-member Court of Appeal bench comprising Justices Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, and K. Muniandy allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence.
The panel ordered that the additional evidence be obtained from prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah through further cross-examination and re-examination.
It also directed that any further evidence introduced by either the defence or prosecution must be confined to matters arising from Rayyan’s additional testimony.
The Court of Appeal further ruled that the additional evidence be taken before a new High Court judge within two weeks of case management, which is scheduled for tomorrow.
Rosmah, the wife of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, sought to adduce the additional evidence, consisting of a police report and a statutory declaration affirmed by Rayyan.
In the declaration, Rayyan allegedly claimed that he had been subjected to pressure from the prosecution during the trial.
On September 1, 2022, the High Court convicted Rosmah on three corruption charges under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
She was found guilty of soliciting RM187.5 million and accepting RM6.5 million in bribes from Saidi Abang Samsudin, the former managing director of Jepak Holdings, through her former aide, Datuk Rizal Mansor.
The bribes were an inducement to help Jepak Holdings secure the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project for 369 rural schools in Sarawak from the Education Ministry.
Rosmah was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment on each charge, to run concurrently, and was also fined RM970 million. She was subsequently granted a stay of execution pending the disposal of her appeal. — Bernama

Title: Former Tabung Haji chairman, CEO among five held over hibah, AMLA probes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Police have detained five people, including a former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and former chief executive officer (CEO), to assist investigations into matters involving the pilgrimage fund.
Commercial Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said three of the suspects were detained over investigations into TH hibah payments made in 2017.
“The other two individuals were detained to assist investigations under Section 4(1) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA),” he said in a statement today.
The five suspects comprise three men and two women aged between 48 and 70, including a former TH chairman, former CEO, former chief financial officer and serving TH personnel.
The three suspects being investigated over the 2017 hibah payments were remanded for two days until tomorrow, while the two investigated under AMLA were remanded for three days until Friday.
Rusdi said investigations were ongoing.
He also urged the public not to speculate or circulate unverified information about the cases, warning that unfounded claims could mislead the public and potentially affect the investigations.
He said the public should obtain information only through official channels.

Title: Haze: Serian records API 213, highest air pollution level in Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Serian in Sarawak continued to record a very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading due to haze this afternoon.
Based on checks on the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the monitoring station at the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD) recorded a reading of 213 as of 4.30 pm.
Eight other areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (186), Kuching (183), Sarikei (174), Miri Industrial Training Institute (166), Samalaju (165), Sri Aman (159), Bintulu (157) and Mukah (151).
Areas with unhealthy air quality in Kuala Lumpur were Batu Muda (169) and Cheras (159); while those in Selangor were Johan Setia (161), Shah Alam (157), Banting (154) and Klang (118); as well as Putrajaya (157).
Also recording unhealthy status were Jerantut (161) and Temerloh (140) in Pahang; Segamat (159), Batu Pahat (155), Kluang (155), Tangkak (152) and Larkin (127) in Johor; Nilai (157), Seremban (155) and Port Dickson (117) in Negeri Sembilan; Tanjung Malim (156) and Tasek Ipoh (154) in Perak; as wel as Bukit Rambai (156), Alor Gajah (152) and Bandaraya Melaka (105) in Melaka.
In total, 31 areas nationwide were reported to be at a moderate level, while five areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 300 and above as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Dengue cases soar 66pc, deaths hit 62 in Malaysia, almost double 2025 toll
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Dengue fever cases nationwide have increased sharply by 66 per cent with 65,979 infections recorded as of Epidemiological Week 35 compared with 39,616 during the same period last year, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The unity government spokesman said the issue was among those discussed at the Cabinet meeting today, with the number of deaths due to dengue also showing a significant increase.
He said 62 cases of deaths due to dengue were recorded up to the 35th epidemiological week of this year, compared to 32 cases in the same period last year.
“The Cabinet was briefed on the status of the dengue problem which showed a marked increase compared with the previous year’s.
“The cumulative death toll for 2025 to the 35th week of the epidemic was 32 cases, while for the same period in 2026 there were 62 cases and this is an increase of 93.8 per cent,” he said at a press briefing that was broadcasted live after the Cabinet meeting in Putrajaya today.
Fahmi, who is also the communications minister, said the Cabinet also discussed measures to address the hike in cases, including the implementation of gotong-royong programmes soon.
He said the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) will be in charge of organising the programme, especially in areas identified as red zones or where an outbreak is occurring.
“The KPKT will start the gotong-royong programme in the next few months, and this will be followed up with a statement from the ministry,” he said.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said the Cabinet was also briefed on the success of the Wolbachia mosquito breeding programme in Putrajaya.
However, he said the Cabinet was also informed about the effects of “fogging” activities on Wolbachia mosquitoes, which are used as a method of dengue control.
“The Wolbachia mosquitoes, which are capable of inhibiting the reproduction and spread of the Aedes mosquito dengue virus, can die during the 'fogging' process.
“With that, efforts to promote gotong-royong programmes need to be given attention, especially in locations identified as high risk,” he said.
The Wolbachia mosquitoes are regular Aedes aegypti mosquitoes that carry a natural, safe bacteria called Wolbachia, which blocks them from spreading dangerous viruses like dengue, Zika, and chikungunya.

Title: Umno says Pakatan applying double standard on royal pardons, points to Anwar’s 2018 case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno today accused Pakatan Harapan (PH) of applying a double standard on royal pardons after the coalition said those convicted in high-profile corruption cases should serve their full sentences.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said PH had supported the full pardon granted to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in 2018 even though he had not completed his five-year prison term at the time.
“If PH could support the pardon granted to Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim even though he had not completed his full sentence at the time, why should a different standard be applied to others?” he said in a statement uploaded on Facebook.
Asyraf also claimed that PH’s statement appeared to question the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s pardoning power, which he said was His Majesty’s prerogative under Article 42(1) of the Federal Constitution.
He said Umno would not pre-empt the Pardons Board’s deliberations or demand any particular outcome.
“Whatever decision is reached through the proper legal process must be respected by all parties,” he said.
Asyraf further said PH had repeatedly belittled and questioned the institution of the Malay Rulers for political gain, which ran contrary to the principles and conditions agreed upon when the unity government was formed.
He said Umno remained committed to defending the institution of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and His Majesty’s constitutional powers.
PH had earlier said those convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, must serve the full sentences imposed by the courts, although it did not name former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak or refer directly to the Pardons Board.
The statement came amid reports that the Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s clemency application when it meets this week.

Title: Fahmi: Malaysia ready to help Indonesia fight forest fires, awaiting green light
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Malaysia is on standby and prepared to assist Indonesia in managing the forest fires that have caused haze in the region, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the Foreign Ministry had briefed the Cabinet on the available assets and conveyed the list to the Indonesian authorities.
“However, until today there has been no updates or confirmation to use Malaysian assets to help extinguish fires,” he said at a press briefing broadcast live after the Cabinet meeting in Putrajaya.
“For us to deploy our assets to assist, we need the permission by the Indonesian authorities,” said Fahmi, who is also the communications minister.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for improvements to the existing Asean mechanism for tackling transboundary haze to ensure such incidents could be addressed effectively.
He said the issue required serious attention from the relevant Asean ministers as the haze threatened public health, particularly that of children and babies.
Forest and peatland fires in Indonesia’s Kalimantan and Sumatra regions have caused severe transboundary haze, with air quality reaching hazardous levels in parts of Malaysia.

Title: MACC: Abdul Azeez chose to remain in purple lock-up attire, handcuffs for court appearance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim chose to wear purple police lock-up attire and handcuffs when he appeared in the Sessions Court here today, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said.
In a statement, the MACC said its officers, the police escorting Abdul Azeez and his lawyer had advised him to change into ordinary clothes before he was taken to court.
“He was also informed that there was no need for him to wear handcuffs,” it said.
However, the MACC said Abdul Azeez insisted on remaining in the lock-up attire and handcuffs until the charge against him had been read.
The commission said that no party, particularly the MACC, had instructed or required him to appear in that manner.
It also urged the public not to speculate or circulate inaccurate information concerning the matter.
Abdul Azeez pleaded not guilty today to using his position as TH chairman to secure the chairmanship of Putrajaya Perdana Berhad and influence TH’s board to approve an investment of up to RM193.5 million in the company in 2014.
He was separately remanded for two days today alongside two former senior TH officials to assist a police investigation into alleged cheating involving the pilgrim fund’s hibah payments.

Title: Cabinet expresses condolences to families of five killed in Sarawak FDS helicopter crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Cabinet today expressed its condolences to the families of the five victims who died in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yesterday.
Unity government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and all ministers offered their sympathies and condolences at the weekly Cabinet meeting today.
“At present, the investigation process is ongoing and the Cabinet will be updated on its progress later," he said at a press briefing broadcast live after the Cabinet meeting in Putrajaya today.
Fahmi, who is also the communications minister, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad had earlier announced the identities of all five victims.
He said the victims’ respective next of kin had been informed of the tragedy.
Fahmi also said the Cabinet had yet to discuss extending assistance to the victims’ families.
“Any further information regarding assistance to the next of kin would be referred to the Health Ministry,” he said.
Yesterday, a German-made MBB BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching, while conducting an FDS operation.
It was reported that CAAM received notification of the crash at 3.58pm.
The pilot, a medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses on board the light, twin-engine, multipurpose utility helicopter were killed.

Title: Malaysian woman held at Delhi airport with 15kg cannabis worth RM2.2m
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — A Malaysian woman was arrested by Indian authorities after she was caught attempting to smuggle 15 kilogrammes of cannabis, valued at approximately 52.5 million rupees (RM2.2 million), at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Sept 4.
Delhi Customs (Airport & General) in a statement on X said the passenger, who arrived from Kuala Lumpur on flight OD-205, was intercepted at Terminal 3 based on profile-based targeting.
"She was diverted at the Green Channel for further inspection. An examination of her trolley bag led to the discovery of 30 polythene pouches containing suspected ganja (cannabis) weighing 15,015.5 grammes (net weight)," the department said.
The suspect was subsequently arrested under Section 43(B) of India’s Narcotics Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, while the illicit drugs were seized under Section 43(A) of the same law.
A case was registered against the Malaysian national under Sections 8, 20, 23, and 29 of the NDPS Act, which deal with the illegal possession, transport, import, and conspiracy involving narcotic substances.  — Bernama
